## What this product is

**Setnayan** (spoken: SET-na-yan, brand-origin phrase *"Set na 'yan."* — Tagalog for "that's all set") is a Philippines-first life-events platform. V1 surface is weddings; the product is built for the broader event market (birthday, celebration, travel, corporate, burial) as event types unlock over time. One app, three role-routed doorways: **customers** plan events end-to-end, **vendors** run a free-during-launch business profile, **admins** (Setnayan team) run operations from a 7-surface internal console. The full 33-iteration spec spine is documented across `0000_*` through `0035_*` folders.

**Papic** (the candid-capture iteration `0012_papic/`) is one of the in-app SKU-driven services within Setnayan. Designated friends/family ("paparazzi") shoot unlimited photos and 5-second clips, tag guests via QR scan, deposit everything into a shared gallery on the couple's existing Setnayan landing page. Every guest gets their tagged photos in real time and can render a 1–30 second personal souvenir reel from a pre-made template library.

**Full Papic spec:** `02_Specifications/10_Papic_Feature_Specification.md` — read it when in doubt.

### Hard product constraints

- **5-second hard cap on video clips.** Capped client-side. Not configurable. UI must enforce.
- **Max 10 tags per photo.** Combined individual + table tags.
- **Untagged-still-delivered guarantee.** Every uploaded photo lands in the couple's gallery regardless of tagging status.
- **Personal Reels:** vertical 9:16 only (1080×1920), 1–30 seconds duration, max 5 guest picks + max 5 couple memorable clips, template-driven render (no per-render AI).
- **Music:** Setnayan-owned AI-generated catalogue only. No major-label music. No per-render music license fee.
- **DSLR pairing is 1 phone : 1 DSLR.** Multi-DSLR-per-phone is V2. WiFi-SDK only in V1; no USB tether.
- **Face detection is per-event-scoped.** Vector store never reused across weddings. Confidence ≥ 0.85 auto-tags; 0.65–0.85 surfaces a suggested tag; below 0.65 the photo uploads untagged.
- **Capture metadata is mandatory.** Every photo and clip stamps `captured_at`, `geo_*` (when fix available), `device_model`, `paired_camera_brand/model` (when paired). Geo is stripped on outbound shares; original on R2 retains it.

## Architecture summary

### Stack

- **Native apps:** iOS 16+ (SwiftUI + AVFoundation), Android 11+ (Compose + CameraX)
- **Backend:** existing Setnayan backend (extend it, don't fork it)
- **Storage:** Cloudflare R2 (PH-region buckets) — hot 90 days, IA cold 5 years
- **Render pipeline:** FFmpeg on Cloudflare Workers + R2 (or Hetzner VM pool fallback)
- **Auth for paparazzi seats:** wedding-scoped ephemeral session tokens via QR-code claim flow (not username/password)
- **QR scanning:** AVFoundation metadata output (iOS) / ML Kit Barcode Scanning (Android)

### Data model (key tables — full schema in spec Part 4.1)

```
Event(event_id, couple_id, paparazzi_tier{3|5}, templates_unlocked[], geolocation_enabled{default true})
PaparazziSeat(seat_id, event_id, claimer_user_id, claim_qr_token)
Guest(guest_id, event_id, assigned_table_id, personal_qr_token)  -- existing in Setnayan
Table(table_id, event_id, table_qr_token)
Photo(photo_id, event_id, paparazzi_seat_id, r2_object_key, type{photo|clip},
       captured_at, geo_lat, geo_lon, geo_accuracy_m, geo_unavailable,
       device_model, paired_camera_brand, paired_camera_model,
       auto_face_attempted, ...)
PhotoTag(photo_id, guest_id, source{individual_qr|table_qr|auto_face|manual_pick}, confidence?, ...)
Template(template_id, feel_category, manifest_json, paired_music_track_ids[])
EventTemplateUnlock(event_id, template_id, purchased_at)
PersonalReel(reel_id, event_id, guest_id, template_id, selected_photo_ids[], r2_output_key)
DslrPairing(pairing_id, event_id, paparazzi_seat_id|live_stream_camera_id,
            brand{canon|nikon|sony|fujifilm}, model, last_paired_at, status)
FaceEnrollment(enrollment_id, event_id, guest_id, source{rsvp_profile|guest_portal|checkin_kiosk},
               vector_blob, quality_score, captured_at, revoked_at?)
```

### Critical flows

**Paparazzi capture → upload → tag:**
1. Native app captures photo/clip → local SQLite WAL
2. Background uploader (BGTaskScheduler/WorkManager) PUTs to R2 via signed URL
3. Tag scanner sheet → scan guest QR (`setnayan:guest:{id}`) or table QR (`setnayan:table:{id}`)
4. Tag intents flush to backend with the upload payload
5. Backend fans out table-tag to all guests assigned to that table (capped at 10 total tags)

**Personal Reel render:**
1. Guest finalizes selections in the landing-page builder
2. POST `/reels/render` with `(event_id, guest_id, template_id, selected_photo_ids, target_duration)`
3. Validate: template unlocked? photos belong to event? guest is RSVP'd?
4. Enqueue render job (Cloudflare Queue)
5. Worker loads template manifest, loads photos+couple-clips+music, generates FFmpeg cmd, encodes 1080×1920 H.264 MP4
6. Output → R2 → notify guest

## Music & template assets

The music catalogue and template library are generated through a separate Cowork-driven workflow — see `14_Music_Catalogue_Cowork_Playbook.md`.

- **Music catalogue:** ~400 owned AI-generated tracks (Suno Premier, generated once, owned forever) across 6 categories — Bridgerton-Feel, Taylor-Swift-Feel, Michael-Jackson-Feel, Jazz, Sunday Morning Vibes, Hip Hop. Stored under `/music_catalogue/{category}/{filename}.mp3`. Manifest at `/music_catalogue/catalogue_manifest.json`.
- **Template library:** ~400 production-ready JSON manifests under `/template_library/{feel_category}/TPL_{nnn}.json`. Master index at `/template_library/library_index.json`. Schema documented in spec Part 4 / playbook Section 12.

When the backend serves a template selection UI to the couple, it reads from `library_index.json`. When the renderer needs music for a render, it picks from the manifest based on the template's `music_pairing_categories` and `music_pairing_bpm_range`.

Per-render cost: ~₱2–₱5 (FFmpeg compute + R2 storage; music free, CDN egress free on R2).

**Live Stream cost is audience-independent.** YouTube absorbs all viewers at ₱0 marginal cost to Setnayan. Per-event cost scales only with camera count and stream duration; whether the wedding has 100 viewers or 1,000,000 viewers, Setnayan's bill is the same.

## Payment system (V1 — apply-then-pay)

Setnayan monetizes via **PHP-direct apply-then-pay** with manual reconciliation. The earlier token-wallet design (iteration 0003) is **retired as of 2026-05-11** — kept on disk for historical context only.

- **Payment rails (V1):** static BDO + GCash receiving accounts owned by Setnayan. Customer applies for a service / order → receives payment instructions email with unique reference code → pays externally → Setnayan Team manually verifies against BDO/GCash inboxes within 24-hr SLA → service activates.
- **PHP-only pricing.** No tokens, no in-app wallet balance, no spending primitive. Each order is a discrete PHP charge tied to a `service_orders` row with `service_key`, `customer_id`, `amount_php`, `reference_code`, `status ∈ pending_payment / paid / failed / refunded`.
- **Setnayan Pay convenience fee:** 3% added to customer invoice when they choose Setnayan as the payment processor for a vendor booking. Vendor receives full booking amount; fee is the customer's cost.
- **V1.5 roadmap:** automated reconciliation via GCash Merchant API (probable) or PayMongo integration (under evaluation). Activation latency drops from 24-hr to minutes.
- **Comp + Unlimited-Use Grants:** admin can issue free-render or unlimited-use grants to specific customer accounts. Grants are a `comp_grant_id` populated on `service_orders` that skip the payment-pending state.
- **Spec convention:** in all .md / .docx specs and design conversations, prices are written in PHP. Only the in-app UI and 0003's own spec talk in tokens directly.

- All-Guest Unlock tier (every guest can shoot via web)
- Native Pro Capture Pack (RAW, manual focus peaking, ISO/shutter)
- Roving Papic service tier (staff photographers)
- Premium Photojournalism + Photo Book
- AI Top-50 same-day curation
- Live Photo Wall venue projection
- Photo Mission system / crew leaderboard
- Cross-paparazzi de-duplication
- BYO music in Personal Reels (CapCut-style client-side render)

These are tracked in spec Part 6. Each is a future spec.

## Privacy & compliance

- PH Data Privacy Act (RA 10173) — guest consent at RSVP, opt-out flow, face-blur for opt-outs, 5-year retention
- Couple has 7-day review window (configurable) before public unlock
- NSFW filter is on by default and CANNOT be disabled
- DPO is the existing Setnayan DPO (registered with NPC)
- Data residency: Cloudflare R2 PH-region buckets

## Common pitfalls / gotchas for engineers

1. **Don't render reels server-side with major-label music.** Even with TOS click-through, server-side rendering makes Setnayan the direct infringer. Catalogue is owned-AI-generated only.
2. **Don't auto-delete photos within 5 years.** PH wedding photographers keep originals 5+ years; we match.
3. **Tag fan-out from table QR.** When a table has 12 guests but cap is 10, alphabetize by RSVP'd name and truncate. Surface the warning to the paparazzo.
4. **Untagged photos still go to the couple.** Don't filter the couple's gallery view by tag presence.
5. **Personal Reel duration is flexible (1–30s) but template slot durations don't all need to scale linearly.** Some templates have minimum slot durations; if guest picks 1s reel from a template with 4s minimum slots, swap to a shorter-template variant or surface an error.
6. **Wedding-scoped session tokens.** A paparazzi seat token only works for its bound event. Don't allow cross-event reuse.
7. **R2 free egress is a real architectural advantage.** Use Cloudflare's CDN end-to-end. Don't proxy through a different cloud unless absolutely necessary.

## Decision log

| Date | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-05-08 | V1 SKUs locked at 3-Paparazzi (₱1,499) and 5-Paparazzi (₱2,499) only | Simplification — drop 8-tier complexity; ship V1 fast |
| 2026-05-08 | Templates priced per-unlock at ₱199 | Couple chooses variety; high-margin upsell; predictable revenue |
| 2026-05-08 | Music catalogue: AI-generated owned (Suno Premier one-time) | Avoid ₱150K/year licensing; no per-render music cost |
| 2026-05-08 | Personal Reel duration: 1–30s flexible (was 30s fixed) | Guest control; template auto-scales slots |
| 2026-05-08 | Template architecture: AI sequencer builds template once per wedding (changed to: pre-made library of 500 templates for V1) | Even more predictable; lookup not generation; faster ship |
| 2026-05-08 | Major-label music: never embedded in renders | Server-side rendering = direct infringer; TOS shield doesn't apply |
| 2026-05-08 | BYO music: deferred to V2 (client-side render only) | CapCut model — only legal path; native-app render needed |
| 2026-05-08 | LED Background offline mode = 5-hour event-length playback via 10-min master loop default (5/10/30 options) | A literal 5-hour 8K MP4 is ~80–110 GB — undeliverable to a venue tech on the day. 10-min loop is ~5.6 GB at 8K, fits on USB; venue's playback system repeats it 30× for the full reception. Photo Pool blend rotates couple's photos per loop iteration so the 30 repeats feel fresh. Custom tier (₱899) supports up to 90-min loops for couples insisting on zero looping. |
| 2026-05-08 | **Token wallet pivot.** All paid services in Setnayan route through a token wallet (iteration 0003). Couples buy packs upfront, spend tokens on services. Multiplier: 30 tokens = ₱1. PHP source of truth; tokens render-time display. "FREE tokens" framing on bonus, never "% off." | Bonus tokens drive larger up-front commitments (5–25% bonus on bigger packs); pull-forward revenue + breakage upside. Real cost of bonus is 1–3% (services run 80–100% margin); likely net positive after factoring breakage |
| 2026-05-08 | **Strict forward iteration sequencing rule.** Each iteration `NNNN` may only depend on iterations `< NNNN`. Forward references are reframed as "this iteration provides X; downstream iterations consume X." Backward dependencies (this iteration depending on a later one) are bugs | Ensures the folder sequence builds cleanly step-by-step. Code-Claude can implement them in numeric order with no circular refs |
| 2026-05-08 | **Cascading rename.** Token Wallet inserted as 0003. Subsequent folders shifted +1: 0003 widgets → 0004; 0004 LED → 0005; 0005 vendors → 0006; 0006 budget → 0007; 0007 seating → 0008; 0008 photo_delivery → 0009; 0009 mood_board → 0010. New: 0011 live_stream, 0012 paparazzi | Sequencing rule required Token Wallet (foundational) to ship before any paid surface |
| 2026-05-08 | Pro Widget pricing bumped from ₱99 → ₱100 and ₱199 → ₱200; Paparazzi from ₱1,499 → ₱1,500 and ₱2,499 → ₱2,500; Templates from ₱199 → ₱200 | Clean × 30 token math (3,000 / 6,000 / 45,000 / 75,000 tokens). Single-peso bumps; couples don't notice |
| 2026-05-08 | **Offline-first design pattern** for all event-day features. Pre-event sync of guest list to paparazzi devices; queued writes for RSVP/check-in/captures; service worker caches invitation site for view-time offline access; LED already offline (USB delivery); Live Stream cannot run truly offline — recommend portable 4G/5G hotspot + auto-fallback to local recording | Filipino wedding venues frequently have weak/no internet. Each event-day iteration includes an "Offline behavior" section in its spec |
| 2026-05-09 | **Custom Monogram Pack at ₱1,999, event-wide.** Renames and rescopes the existing Live Stream "Custom Overlay + Custom Standby" SKU. One purchase replaces the Setnayan logo with the couple's monogram across all media outputs: Live Stream broadcast + recordings, Paparazzi photo exports, Personal Reels, gallery chrome, future surfaces. 4 overlay designs × portrait/landscape variants = 8 layouts. Auto-generated default monogram if couple doesn't upload PNG. Registered as a service in 0003 wallet (`custom_monogram_pack`). | Aspirational ("your monogram on your wedding's media") not defensive ("pay to remove ours"). Preserves Setnayan marketing surface in default state; couples self-select to upgrade. Pricing parity with Live Stream's existing ₱1,999 SKU; one purchase covers all features. |
| 2026-05-09 | **Paparazzi rear camera only — front camera disabled by design.** | Photo quality: rear cameras have larger sensors, better optics, more usable resolution. Paparazzi shoot other people, not themselves — front camera has no use case. Removed flip button from action row; replaced with Pick (manual guest picker) shortcut. |
| 2026-05-09 | **Paparazzi gesture shutter — 4 modes via direction.** Tap = photo. Drag up = photo with flash. Drag right = 5-sec clip. Drag right → drag up (chord, before release) = 5-sec clip with flash. Mode pill removed; gesture itself selects the mode. | Cleaner UX than tap-vs-hold. Flash decision baked into the gesture, not a separate toggle. Diagonal "drag upper-right" rejected in favor of the chord (right-then-up) — easier to execute precisely than diagonal. |
| 2026-05-09 | **Paparazzi V1 trims.** Cut from V1 (deferred to 0013 V1.1 Polish): Photo Center curator role (no human owner at most events), wedding-day profile photo auto-update (face match works without it), extended sort/filters (V1 ships 4 essentials only — chronological / photos of us / untagged / type), battery escalation tiers at 10% and 5% (V1 ships only the 20% warning + manual handoff QR), delivered-status indicator + couple nudge. Kept in V1: bulk hide/unhide for the 7-day review window. | V1 was scope-creeping into a heavier product than needed. Trimmed to ship what wins the market — native rear-only candid capture, QR tagging, untagged-still-delivered, monogram branding, real-time delivery. Polish layer ships in 0013 once we have launch data. |
| 2026-05-09 | **Paparazzi storage default: app sandbox only, no auto-save to camera roll.** Opt-in toggle in settings to save copies; defaults off. After upload + 24h grace, local sandbox copy is purged. "My contributions" post-event view per paparazzo for personal copies. | Privacy-respecting default — guests' candid photos shouldn't sit in random friends' personal albums by default. Local SQLite WAL stays for retroactive tagging. Opt-in keeps the door open for friends who want their work as a portfolio piece. |
| 2026-05-09 | **Paparazzi battery handoff at 20% only (V1).** Single warning threshold; manual handoff QR mirrors Live Stream slot takeover (3-second grace, session token revoke + reissue). | Three-tier escalation (20% / 10% / 5% with crew push + auto-pause) was over-engineered for V1. Single warning + manual handoff covers 95% of cases. V1.1 adds the escalations once we see real event data. |
| 2026-05-09 | **Iteration drafting workflow locked.** Each iteration produces a folder `NNNN_short_topic_slug/` with three files sharing the iteration base name: `.md` (engineering spec), `.html` (web + mobile mockup using the canvas pattern from 0001), `.docx` (mirrors md content). Drafted both 0011 (Live Stream) and 0012 (Paparazzi) this session. | Memory rule: Setnayan deliverables ship web + mobile parity in every iteration. Three formats serve three audiences: md for engineering, html for design review, docx for stakeholder review. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0007 Budget & Expenses scope lock.** Three line items per vendor (Package, Crew Meal, Transportation), each with own deadline (couple-input in V1) and payment log. Payment records capture amount, date, method, reference, proof screenshot. Vendor's GCash/Maya/bank QR displayed per line for one-tap scan-to-pay (sourced from 0006). Rollup cards: total / paid / balance / next due. Calendar export via .ics (universal — Apple/Google/Outlook); default reminders 24h + 1h before deadline. Setnayan platform costs auto-populate from 0003 wallet (read-only). Misc free-form expenses supported. PHP only; no targets, no forecasting, no categories, no external sharing in V1. | User's stated goal was to curate every amount needing settlement — 3-line structure maps to actual Filipino vendor billing patterns. .ics over native EventKit/CalendarContract because no permissions/OAuth needed; works everywhere. Couple-only access matches existing wallet model. Targets/forecasting/multi-currency/sharing all V1.1+ candidates once we see usage data. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0007 calendar duplicate-avoidance — two layers.** Layer 1: stable VEVENT UIDs (`{event_id}-{line_item_id}@setnayan.ph`) so Apple/Google/Outlook update existing events on re-import instead of duplicating. Layer 2: per-line `tracked_in_calendar` boolean toggle. Bulk "Add all due dates" only exports lines flagged false; button text adapts ("Add 5 new dates" / "All on calendar — re-export?"). Couple manually toggles in either direction. | True calendar read access requires native app + permission OR OAuth per provider — V2 scope. The two-layer V1 approach gets ~95% of the value without the integration cost. UID dedup handles re-import duplicates automatically; manual flag handles cases where couple added to calendar outside Setnayan. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0010 Mood Board V1 — palettes only, Setnayan Guide rule engine.** Every guest-list role + venue gets a 6-color palette. Color input via hex / picker / name autocomplete (~300-entry library) / image extraction. 20 pre-template themes (Style: Classic/Pastel/Royalty/Nomadic/Sweet/Elegant/Dreamy/Muted/Boho · Color-led: Blue/Red/Green/Gold/Baby Blue/Army/Pink · Seasonal: Spring/Summer/Autumn/Winter). Setnayan Guide rule engine evaluates 7 categories on every change: cohesion (8-color hard limit + 60-30-10 soft target), contrast (per-tier minimums + inversion check), background-vs-foreground proximity (ΔE 10), temperature consistency, saturation hierarchy, photography color cast, cultural defaults (PH bride white/ivory + sponsor pairing). Engine returns pass/warn/contradict states with structured suggestions. Disable toggle per-event (default ON) and per-palette ("Use this color anyway"). Master palette dedups by hex AND named color. Stylist persona, inspirations paste board, role outfit galleries, venue segments with photos/videos, concept-vs-actual all DEFERRED until stylist persona exists (V2 / Din). Saved palettes V1=couple-scoped, schema-ready for stylist scope V2. Mobile thumb-zone UX (all primary touch targets in lower third). | Engine baseline grounded in color theory + WCAG contrast ratios + wedding photography best practice + PH cultural conventions. Opinionated by design — couples save themselves photos that don't work. Override paths for couples who want full control. 20 themes parallel content workstream like 400 Reel templates and music catalogue; iteration code consumes via JSON manifest. Couple-scoped saved palettes today, stylist-scoped library lights up later when stylists exist (Din Phase 3). |
| 2026-05-09 | **0006 Vendors taxonomy: hybrid (28 canonical + per-event custom).** Canonical list spans typical PH wedding services (ceremony/reception venues, catering, photo, video, SDE, drone, prenup, coordination, HMUA, gowns, suits, florals, cake, lights & sound, DJ/emcee, mobile bar, live band, acoustic performer, choir/quartet, officiant, bridal car, guest shuttle, invitation print, stationery/signage, photobooth, souvenirs, rings, honeymoon planner). Couples mark canonical services "not needed" or add custom rows scoped per event. | Canonical spine drives clean coverage reporting and predictable rollup into Budget (0007). Custom rows handle the long tail without forcing a "request canonical addition" gate. Per-event scoping keeps the global list clean. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0006 vendor payment model: flexible custom milestones, not fixed 3-stage.** Each vendor has any number of milestones with custom labels, due dates, amounts, paid status, payment method/reference. UI presets scaffold "Reservation + Down + Balance," "4 partials + Balance," "Lump sum" patterns. Balance + payment progress + overdue flag computed; surfaced in list and detail views. **Note:** 0007 Budget overlays this with a 3-line view (Package / Crew Meal / Transportation) for top-level budget UX; the underlying milestone schema in 0006 stays flexible. | PH wedding vendors structure schedules differently — fixed 3-stage forces couples to lie about reality. Schema flexibility costs little; UI presets keep entry fast for the common case. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0006 crew meals: count × per-meal cost = computed total**, with `vendor_provides_meals` toggle that zeroes contribution without losing headcount. Defaults to event-level rate (set once on catering vendor); editable per-vendor. Rolls up to event aggregate; consumed by 0007 Budget as the "Crew Meal" line per vendor. | Couple needs the rolled-up number for catering headcount and the budget. The opt-out matters because larger vendors sometimes bring their own crew meals. Don't double-count — vendor packages are separate budget rows. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0006 vendor payments are tracking-only — NOT integrated with token wallet (0003).** Vendor money leaves Setnayan (cash/GCash/bank transfer direct to vendor). Setnayan records what couple says they paid; never validates the transaction. Wallet stays reserved for Setnayan-charged services (Pro widgets, Paparazzi, Templates, Monogram, Live Stream, LED). Combined views live in Budget (0007), which reads vendor milestones + wallet spend without coupling them. | Mixing external vendor payments into the wallet would blur the source-of-truth boundary. Couples already think in two buckets: "what I paid the vendor" vs "what I paid Setnayan." Keep them separate; combine at the reporting layer. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0006 manual encoding only in V1; vendor self-input deferred to Din (Phase 3 supplier app).** Vendors are external; their accounts and inputs land in Din. V1's vendor records are couple-encoded and inherit cleanly into Din with no migration. | Building a half-baked vendor login surface in V1 would block launch and create a migration we'd then have to throw away. Couple-encoded data is sufficient for the planning workflow. Din ships in Phase 3 with the same backend records. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0006 meetings module added to vendor profiles.** Each vendor has a list of scheduled meetings (initial consult, tasting, walkthrough, fitting, etc.) with title, datetime, mode (in-person/video/phone), location/link, agenda, attendees, post-meeting notes. Soonest upcoming surfaces as "Next meeting" on the vendor card; past-but-still-scheduled renders amber and prompts confirmation. `vendor_meetings` table includes a `created_by_actor` column ('couple' in V1) so Din (Phase 3) can later write 'vendor' rows into the same table without migration. No .ics export in 0006 — that lives in 0007 Budget which already owns the calendar pattern. | Couples currently track meetings in scattered notes and message threads. Centralizing on the vendor profile mirrors how planners actually work. The forward-compatibility column makes Din's takeover data-only. .ics in 0007 means one combined feed (payments + meetings) instead of two. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 Seating Chart table catalog locked at 13 entries.** Round (8/10/12), Long banquet (6/8/10), Family head — long rectangular (12/14/16), Sweetheart (2), Serpentine (10/14/18). Family head tables are explicitly **long rectangulars, not ovals** — sized larger than the standard long banquet and reserved for the immediate family of the bride or groom. Capacity is bound to type — no per-table custom-capacity in V1. Custom shapes deferred to V1.1. | Covers 95%+ of Filipino reception venues. Avoids the rabbit hole of arbitrary geometry; serpentine added explicitly because Filipino entourage tables often use it; family-head ovals were a visual mistake — Filipino venues stock these as long banquet tables, not oval tops. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 floor plan carries full venue elements**, not just tables. Stage is required; band platform is optional (adjacent to or on the stage); dancefloor is an optional rectangle in front of the stage that no tables may sit inside; at least one main entrance door is required by Publish (side / service doors optional). Doors snap to walls only and render as arched gaps in the wall line. | The seating chart is the canonical reception layout, used by Print pack signs and by Paparazzi (0012) for orientation. Modeling stage / band / dancefloor / doors as first-class elements means the print-pack overview reads as a real floor plan rather than just a table grid. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 venue dimensions are optional.** Couples who already know their venue size flip a toolbar toggle to set room width × length in metres; the editor then renders walls at scale and bounds placement (no tables outside walls, on doors, or on the dancefloor). Couples who don't know yet leave it blank — placement is fully free-form, the canvas grows to fit content, no walls are drawn. Couples can set or clear at any time. | Forcing dimensions upfront would block planning for couples who book the venue but haven't measured it. Free-form is the early-planning default; bounded mode is a precision affordance for the home stretch. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 rotation rule by shape.** Round, sweetheart, family-head: rotation locked at 0°. Long banquet (`long_*`) and serpentine (`serpentine_*`): rotation in **45° increments** (0/45/90/135/180/225/270/315). | Filipino venues are rarely orthogonal — couples need 45° steps to align friend / entourage tables to non-orthogonal walls and aisles. Round and sweetheart don't benefit from rotation; family-head tables sit perpendicular to the stage by convention. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 alignment lock on by default.** Dragging a table reveals pink horizontal and vertical guide lines that snap the moving table's center, top edge, or left edge to the same coordinate as nearby stationary tables. Toggleable in the toolbar; complementary to (not a replacement for) the 10-pt grid snap. | Without alignment guides, a 60-table reception ends up with subtle misalignments that look bad in the printed overview. Lock-on-default mirrors how Figma / Sketch behave; couples turn it off only for pixel-precise edge cases. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 chair-level interaction.** Every table renders chairs as small circles around the perimeter — one per seat. Filled with profile photo when available; with two-letter initials on a side-coded gradient when not. Empty seats render dashed-outline white. **Gestures:** tap chair = swap that guest's seat (single-seat move); long-press chair = open guest details; tap table body = swap that whole table's position with another (everyone seated stays with their table); long-press table = table settings. Initials-only chairs surface the full name on selection via a floating name pop and a sticky banner at the top of the canvas. | The chair-circle model mirrors how couples actually think about seating — by person, not by abstract slot. Splitting tap (swap) from long-press (details) keeps the primary interaction (move someone to a different seat) one-handed and fast. The dual hit-zone (chair circles vs. table body) lets a single tap gesture mean two different things without a mode switch. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 serpentine geometry locked.** A serpentine segment is a quarter-donut wedge — one quarter of a ring — with **2 inner-cove chairs + 4 outer-edge chairs = 6 seats per segment**. Couples assemble multiple segments into C-shapes, U-cups, and longer arcs. Catalog ships 1/2/3-segment configurations (`serpentine_6` / `serpentine_12` / `serpentine_18` = 6/12/18 seats). Serpentines are **resizable in place** via the table-detail sheet — adding or removing a segment without deleting and re-creating the table; capacity = `6 × segments`. Earlier representations (S-curve strokes, line-only paths) were wrong — serpentines are real banded tables with width, fillet, and chairs on both inside and outside. | Matches reference photos of real Filipino-wedding entourage tables. The 2+4 chair pattern is dictated by the donut geometry: the inner arc is shorter, fits ~2; the outer arc is longer, fits ~4. Locking this prevents future "let's make it 5 chairs" drift, and the segment-based capacity makes the resize affordance trivial to spec. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 stage placement is free anywhere on the canvas.** Top, bottom, left, right edge, or true center for in-the-round receptions. Auto-fill ring distances recompute around wherever the stage lands. | Real Filipino venues run all four orientations plus the occasional in-the-round. Locking the stage to one edge would force couples to mentally rotate every venue into our model. |
| 2026-05-09 | **0008 auto-fill uses role-tier rings centered on the stage.** Tier 1 (principal sponsors + officiant + immediate family) innermost; Tier 2 (entourage + secondary sponsors + bearers + flower girl) second; Tier 3 (extended family) third; Tier 4 (friends, work, school) outermost. | 2026-05-14 | **Caching & Offline Strategy locked.** Hard 100 MB per-user/per-install storage budget gated by `navigator.storage.estimate()` at startup (drops to 50% of available headroom if browser reports < 100 MB free). Allocation: ~75 MB images · ~20 MB JSON/data · ~5 MB headroom; splits soft, LRU within each layer. Two-layer architecture: (1) **Data layer** = TanStack Query + `persistQueryClient` to IndexedDB with stale-while-revalidate, per-query TTL, hard `maxAge` (7 days), and `buster` key bumped per schema change; (2) **Asset layer** = service worker (`apps/web/public/sw.js`) with route-scoped `CacheExpiration` (`maxEntries` + `maxAgeSeconds`) for images (500 entries / 30 days), JS chunks (100 entries / 7 days, stale-while-revalidate), fonts (20 entries / 1 year). **MUST cache:** app shell, JS chunks, fonts, public-read data (events, guests, vendor profiles, mood board, schedule, budget, save-the-date assets). **MUST NEVER cache:** auth tokens, Supabase session, payment intents, BIR receipts, contract files, API-gateway per-request-key responses, live chat (use Realtime). **Invalidation discipline:** every mutation MUST invalidate its query key — enforced via `useTrackedMutation` wrapper around `useMutation` with required `invalidates: QueryKey[]` field + ESLint rule `setnayan/no-raw-mutation` blocking raw `useMutation` in feature code. **Stale-time defaults** (overridable per query): hot lists (guests, day-of schedule) 60s · warm data (vendor profiles, mood board, budget) 5min · cold/immutable (BIR receipts, finalized themes) 1hr. **Eviction:** LRU per layer (assets by `lastAccessedAt`, data by `dataUpdatedAt`); no cross-layer fallback. **Out of scope:** native iOS/Android offline (Phase 2) · photo gallery archive downloads (0009 handles via direct R2 signed URLs + native share, not the PWA cache) · music catalogue files (R2 HTTP cache, not service worker). Canonical spec at `02_Specifications/Caching_and_Offline_Strategy.md`. Acceptance criteria for Sprint 0 validation: cold visit <1.5s on 4G (Lighthouse mobile) · warm return renders cached guest list <100ms before revalidation · quota-hit LRU verified by programmatic 75 MB fill test · schema buster wipes persisted blob on bump · ESLint rule blocks merge on raw `useMutation` · automated audit asserts no auth/payment/receipt/contract content in IndexedDB or SW caches · 200-guest day-of stress test bounds network with 60s staleTime. | Solves two predictable failure modes for return visits to a planning-tool app couples will use over 6–18 months: (1) cold start latency — returning users opening their dashboard shouldn't wait on network to see their guest list, they should see the last-known state in <100ms with background revalidation; (2) unbounded storage bloat — a user who has accumulated a year of vendor portraits, mood-board thumbs, and save-the-date previews shouldn't end up with 500 MB of Setnayan assets eating device storage. Two-layer split keeps eviction reasoning local — image churn doesn't pressure the data cache and vice versa. Sensitive data exclusion (auth, payment intents, BIR receipts, contracts) is non-negotiable for PH legal compliance + RA 10173. Mutation-invalidation wrapper makes the discipline impossible to bypass, which matters because cache-related bugs are notoriously hard to diagnose in production — surfacing them at lint time prevents shipping them. Consumed by iterations 0013 (platform stack) · 0021/0022/0023 (dashboards) · 0031 (day-of guest, offline-first PWA shell) · 0035 (observability emits `cache_layer` + `cache_outcome` metrics to PostHog without including cached content). |

| 2026-05-15 | **Dual-role customer ↔ vendor — self-purchase confirm + self-review hard-gate (locked).** Extends "one app, three role-routed entries" (2026-05-11) and the § 10a internal-account pattern (2026-05-12) explicitly to the customer ↔ vendor surface: a single `users` row may carry `account_type='vendor'` AND own/host events as a customer. Vendor application is **additive** — applying never closes the customer surface; event creation, cart, and booking flows stay open and the Switch-view pill toggles between the two roles (same shape as admin = customer-with-admin-grants per § 10a). **Self-purchase confirm step (at checkout).** When any `cart_items` row resolves to a `vendor` whose `owner_user_id = auth.uid()` OR whose `vendor_service_agents.member_id` includes `auth.uid()`, the cart inserts a confirm modal with two CTAs: **"Pay full price"** (standard payment flow, no special treatment, no discount) OR **"Comp for myself"** (skip payment-pending; new `comp_grants.source='vendor_self_comp'`, audit-logged, single-admin authority via 0023, rate-limited to 12 comps per vendor per quarter — admin can raise the cap with reason logged). Self-comp orders are excluded from vendor-side conversion analytics so vendor dogfooding does not inflate their reported numbers. **Self-review HARD-gated at three layers.** (1) **Schema:** CHECK constraint `no_self_review` plus `BEFORE INSERT` trigger `block_related_account_review()` on `vendor_reviews` that refuses the row when reviewer shares ANY of [vendor ownership (`vendors.owner_user_id`), team membership (`vendor_service_agents.member_id`), payment method (matching `service_order_payments.payer_account_number`), device fingerprint (matching new `user_devices.device_hash`), household address (matching new `users.address_normalized`)] with the vendor owner OR any team member. (2) **API:** `POST /api/v1/reviews` catches the trigger exception and returns `403 SELF_REVIEW_BLOCKED` with `matched_signal ∈ {owner_self, team_member, payment_match, device_match, household_match}` and `next_action: "contest_via_help"`. (3) **UI:** the "Leave a review" CTA renders disabled with hint *"You can't review your own services"* on the booked-vendor card when the event flips to Wrap stage; tap-on-disabled opens the appeal flow. **Appeal path.** Filipino households legitimately share GCash numbers, devices, and addresses, so the gate WILL produce false positives. Customer contests via 0023 Help inbox → admin investigates (genuine related-account vs. coincidental shared payer reference) → admin override-publishes the review with reason logged in `admin_audit_log`. Single-admin authority; falls below the two-admin threshold per § 9.1. **Admin parity.** Admins are already customers carrying `is_internal=TRUE` (§ 10a); the self-review gate applies symmetrically — an admin who books a vendor on the customer side cannot review that vendor if the admin sits on the vendor's team. **Schema additions to support the gate:** new table `user_devices (user_id, device_hash, last_seen_at)` (1 row per (user, device) pair, populated on session-start) and new column `users.address_normalized TEXT` (computed from existing address fields, lowercased + whitespace-collapsed for matching; null-safe in the trigger — match never fires on null). | Closes the fake-review fraud vector (vendor astroturfs own product with 5-star reviews) without blocking legitimate self-purchase. A flat ban on self-purchase taxes honest vendors (grand opening dogfooding, internal booking-flow QA, gifting a service to a friend's event) and pushes determined fraudsters to second accounts anyway — harder to detect than a same-account purchase. The surgical fix gates the **review**, not the **purchase**, because the review is where the harm actually lands on the marketplace's decision quality. Hard-gating cross-account at review time (vs. logged-not-gated in moderation) was the owner's call on 2026-05-15: false-positive risk on legit dual-account households is acceptable because (a) the moderation appeal path is cheap (single-admin override-publish via 0023 Help inbox), and (b) the inverse — letting fake reviews land and removing them later — has already polluted the marketplace decision the review was supposed to inform. Confirm modal with two CTAs (vs. flat "always full price") lets vendors self-comp when dogfooding their own checkout, with an audit trail that prevents the comp from becoming a budget hack; the 12/quarter rate-limit anchors the cap somewhere reasonable for a launch vendor and admin can raise it for documented cases. Excluding self-comp orders from vendor analytics keeps reported conversion honest. Mirrors the admin dual-role pattern from § 10a: one `users` row, multiple roles, real customer codepath with safeguards at the harm point rather than at the entry. | `CLAUDE.md` decision log, `0006_vendors_management/0006_vendors_management.md` (Reviews schema: `no_self_review` CHECK + `block_related_account_review()` BEFORE INSERT trigger + new § "Dual-role customer ↔ vendor — review gate"), `0034_payments_and_cart/0034_payments_and_cart.md` (new § 3.1a Self-purchase confirm modal + new § 10c Vendor self-comp grant type + `comp_grants.source` CHECK expanded with `vendor_self_comp` + new `user_devices (user_id, device_hash, last_seen_at)` table + new `users.address_normalized` column), `0021_couple_dashboard_fully_purchased/0021_couple_dashboard_fully_purchased.md` (§ 2.2d table: new row "Self-review (vendor owner / team member viewing own bookings)" — always blocked, appeal copy), `0023_admin_console/0023_admin_console.md` (new § Review moderation queue with related-account signals column + override-publish action under single-admin authority; § 3.3 Payments queue: self-purchase + self-comp flag badges; surface for adjusting per-vendor self-comp quarterly rate-limit). **`.docx` mirrors NOT regenerated** (pandoc unavailable in current environment) — flag for next Cowork session. **Implementation pending** — backend migration (CHECK + trigger + `user_devices` table + `users.address_normalized` column + `comp_grants.source` CHECK extension + `service_order_payments.payer_account_number` column added) and UI (cart confirm modal + disabled review CTA + admin appeal flow + self-comp rate-limit surface) deferred to engineering worktree. |

| 2026-05-15 | **Vendor public-visibility state machine + Website editor widget architecture (locked).** Two coupled decisions extending the morning's stack. **(1) Vendor public-visibility correction.** Vendors who have registered but are not yet verified now show on the public marketplace as **"Coming soon"** cards instead of being hidden. New column `vendors.public_visibility ENUM('hidden','coming_soon','verified','archived') DEFAULT 'coming_soon'` (iteration 0022 § 2.1c). States: `coming_soon` (default at registration · profile publicly listed with muted "Coming soon" badge · no booking CTA · read-only preview) → `verified` (set by admin via Verification Queues 0023 § 3.2 · fully bookable) · `hidden` (admin suspension / withdrawal · not surfaced anywhere) · `archived` (terminal · removed from browse · existing relationships preserve referential integrity). DIY-mode marketplace browse popup (0006 § DIY-mode filter popup) gains a **"Verified only"** toggle OFF by default — couples see both states; toggle ON filters to verified-only. **`verified_vendor_count` metric** (Section 3 stats threshold + Section 1 announcement bar auto-hide + boost-service launch gate 2026-05-14) continues to count only `public_visibility='verified'` rows; `coming_soon` vendors are visible publicly but do NOT contribute to the verification-count threshold metrics. Three gate types: `NULL` (always-on widget) · `'count'` (gated by count thresholds — Section 3 stats) · `'per_tile'` (per-tile visibility — Section 12 platforms). **V1 admin-editable fields:** `is_enabled` + `display_order` ONLY. Per-widget config (stats thresholds · platform store URLs · copy overrides · A/B variants) stays code-locked in V1; admin editing of `config` JSONB deferred to V1.1. **Admin Website editor surface at `/admin/website`** (iteration 0023 § 3.10) — list of widgets per page · drag-drop reorder · enable/disable toggle · audit-logged via `admin_audit_log` actions `site_widgets_toggle` / `site_widgets_reorder` · single-admin authority per § 4.3 · mobile lives under "More" tab. **Iteration 0023 admin surface count 7 → 8** (§ 1 table extended with new row 8). **Replaces** the standalone `site_visibility_flags` table from the morning's stats-gating entry — folded into `site_widgets.is_enabled` + the derived `count_gate_passes` check on `gate_type='count'` widgets. `platform_availability` table (Section 12 per-tile detail) stays as sibling table linked logically to `home_platforms` widget by convention. | Two drivers. **First**, the vendor `public_visibility` default shift from `hidden` → `coming_soon` addresses the chicken-and-egg problem of a launching marketplace: pre-verification vendors who completed registration but haven't yet been admin-reviewed need somewhere to land that's neither "fully bookable" nor "invisible." A "Coming soon" surface state lets couples see real coverage forming on the marketplace before the verified vendor pool reaches critical mass, while honestly signaling that the vendor isn't yet bookable. Honest-but-visible beats hidden-until-perfect for two reasons: couples gain confidence the platform is growing; vendors are incentivized to complete verification quickly to flip status. The `verified` count metrics (Section 3 stats gate, announcement bar auto-hide, boost-service launch gate) stay strict — `coming_soon` vendors don't count toward thresholds — so trust signals remain honest. **Second**, the widget architecture refactor was already implicit in the morning's per-section gating tables (`site_visibility_flags` for Section 3, `platform_availability` for Section 12); generalizing it to all 12 sections gives admins a single place to manage marketing-site composition without separate per-section toggles in code. Limiting V1 admin scope to `is_enabled` + `display_order` (not config / copy / variants) keeps the editor surface tight while solving the immediate need (turn sections off when they're not yet relevant; reorder for A/B if needed). The decision NOT to support per-widget config editing in V1 is deliberate — keeping the iteration spec as the source of truth for content means engineering doesn't have to build a "marketing CMS" that competes with spec authority. Save-the-Date "social-native clip" (15s teaser MP4 for IG Reels / TikTok) deferred to V1.1+ as an optional add-on; couples in V1 share the landing-page link (Open Graph card renders beautifully on FB / WhatsApp; lower reach on IG / TikTok accepted as V1 launch tradeoff). | Three drivers. **First**, the video-file primitive was the wrong fit for the actual job-to-be-done. | 2026-05-16 | **Monogram Hero PNG-to-SVG conversion via Potrace · amends earlier SVG-only-hard-block stance.** Second 2026-05-16 row, amendment to the first. The earlier entry's *"PNG monogram uploads rejected at upload time for the Monogram Hero upgrade"* hard block is **softened** to a **hybrid policy with preview gate**: PNG uploads are accepted, server-side Potrace conversion runs, the couple sees a preview of the converted SVG + trace animation, and the couple explicitly approves the converted version before checkout proceeds. **Locked flow (6 steps):** (1) Couple in Monogram Hero checkout, has PNG monogram. (2) Editor offers "Convert your PNG to SVG so it can animate? We'll show you the result first." (3) Couple taps Convert → server runs Potrace via Cloudflare Worker (WASM build) → ~2 second wait. (4) Preview screen: side-by-side original PNG + animated SVG trace preview (looping ~3s). (5) Three CTAs: **Use this SVG · Try a different file · Use auto-generated instead**. (6) On *Use this SVG*: checkout proceeds with the converted SVG stored as canonical (`hero_monogram.converted_svg_url`); **PNG original kept as backup** under `hero_monogram.uploaded_url` for audit / archive / future re-conversion if Potrace settings improve. **Engine choice: Potrace (open-source).** Wrapped as a Cloudflare Worker WASM function. Free per conversion (~₱0 marginal cost). Mature, battle-tested (Inkscape's Trace Bitmap is built on it). Quality 80–90% on high-contrast monogram-style content. Alternatives considered + rejected: Vectorizer.ai API (~₱11/conversion, vendor lock-in), ImageTracerJS (lower quality), Adobe Image Trace API (overkill + expensive). **No-refund clause still stands** for the Monogram Hero SKU — the preview gate IS the consent mechanism (couple sees exactly what they're paying for before commit), so all-sales-final remains morally defensible. **Schema additions to `hero_monogram.config_json`:** `converted_svg_url` (R2 path to Potrace output), `converted_svg_approved_at` (ISO timestamp of couple's preview-gate approval), `converted_svg_potrace_settings` (threshold / turdsize / optcurve / opttolerance — captured for reproducibility if we re-run conversion with improved defaults). **API integration:** Potrace WASM build deployed as a Cloudflare Worker function (`/api/monogram/convert`); reads PNG from R2 `setnayan-media`, writes SVG to same bucket under `hero_monogram/{event_id}/converted.svg`, returns preview-renderable URL. Engineering effort ~3 days (Potrace WASM compile + Worker wiring + preview-gate UI in the upgrade flow + acceptance approval write to schema). | The earlier hard-block was the right *default* but unnecessarily restrictive on what is technically possible. Many couples receive their monogram as PNG from their wedding-branding designer (the designer keeps the SVG source); forcing those couples to either (a) go back to the designer for SVG, (b) use auto-generated instead, or (c) skip the ₱1,999 upgrade entirely all leak conversion. The preview gate protects the quality bar without locking out couples who only have PNG — they self-select away from bad conversions because they see the result before paying. Potrace specifically (vs the commercial alternatives) keeps marginal cost at ₱0, which protects the 95%+ margin on the ₱1,999 SKU. The 10% of conversions that look mediocre will be revealed at the preview gate and rejected by the couple before payment; the no-refund clause therefore stays clean. PNG-as-backup is a low-cost safety net (PNG is small; R2 storage cost negligible) that enables future re-conversion if we improve Potrace settings or add a better engine in V1.1+. | `CLAUDE.md` decision log (this entry); `0004_invitation_widgets/0004_invitation_widgets.md` (`hero_monogram` schema extended with conversion fields; Monogram Hero purchase flow rewritten to surface the 6-step preview-gate path instead of the SVG-required hard-block; the earlier *"SVG-only: PNG monogram uploads rejected at upload time"* line replaced with the hybrid policy; acceptance criteria updated to test the conversion + preview-approval flow); `API_Integration_Checklist.md` (new Tier 5 entry — Potrace WASM build + Cloudflare Worker deploy + R2 routing); ~~`0002_qr_invitation_system/0002_qr_invitation_system.md`~~ no edit needed (mentions "SVG-only" only in passing reference to 0004's rules). **`.docx` mirrors NOT regenerated** (pandoc unavailable). **Engineering implementation pending** — Potrace WASM compile (npm `potrace-wasm` exists; verify size + license); Cloudflare Worker `/api/monogram/convert` endpoint; preview-gate UI component in the Monogram Hero checkout step (side-by-side PNG vs animated SVG trace); schema migration for the 3 new `hero_monogram` config fields. **Sequencing note:** Amends the first 2026-05-16 row's *"SVG-only no fallback"* line; both rows together describe the final V1 Monogram Hero policy. |
| 2026-05-16 | **Papic V1.5+ architecture lock — 207-camera mesh · Drive transfer at T+30d · cold-tier 90-day safety window · 150-credit/guest · Auto-Recap (FFmpeg no-AI) · pooled credit pool 5K/10K · ALL Papic SKUs deferred to V1.5+ but architecture frozen now.** Third 2026-05-16 row. Papic V1 native iOS/Android build is **deferred to V1.5+** (no V1 engineering bandwidth for native apps) but the architecture is **locked now** so the V1.5+ build cannot re-litigate decisions already argued through. **(1) 207-camera per event** = 5 paid paparazzi + 200 guest cameras + couple seat; each guest gets **150 captured-photo credits**, bundled free in the Premium Guest Camera Pack. **(2) Drive transfer at T+30d** — couple OAuths their Google account; Setnayan pushes the full archive (photos, videos, Auto-Recap, XMP/EXIF metadata) to the couple's `Setnayan/[Event Name]/` folder root. Couple owns the archive from T+30d onward. **(3) Cold-tier 90-day safety window** — Setnayan retains a cold-tier R2 mirror from T+30d through T+120d (cuts long-tail storage cost ~80% vs hot-tier indefinite retention); after T+120d cold-tier lapses and the couple's own Drive is canonical. **(4) XMP/EXIF tag embedding on Drive transfer** — face-tags, table tags, capture timestamp, geo coordinates, photographer ID embedded into XMP sidecars per-photo + EXIF UserComment where supported, so Lightroom / Photo Mechanic / Capture One / Photos.app read metadata natively; | 2026-05-16 | **Panood V1 SKU lock — drop Cloudflare Stream Live composite · BYO YouTube via OAuth · per-day pricing (Daily Broadcast ₱499 · Camera Sync ₱99) · Annual Streaming ₱2,999 / Annual Streaming Plus ₱3,999.** Fourth 2026-05-16 row. **Architecture pivot:** drop the Cloudflare Stream Live SFU + server-side ffmpeg compositor + RTMP relay through Setnayan's master `@SetnayanWeddings` channel. Replace with **couple's own YouTube channel via OAuth** — couple grants Setnayan YouTube Live write permission to *their* channel, Setnayan provides the broadcaster web UI + multi-cam switching + auto landing-page embed, but the video stream lives on the couple's YouTube forever. Setnayan never composites or relays; the broadcaster UI pushes one active feed at a time to the couple's YouTube via standard RTMP from the currently-selected camera, and multi-cam switching is the operator tapping between phone feeds inside the Setnayan broadcaster UI. **(1) Daily Broadcast** ₱499/day (per-day multi-purchase — couples buy as many days as they need: prep day + ceremony day + reception day = 3 days × ₱499 = ₱1,497). **(2) Camera Sync** ₱99/day (Panood multi-cam only — unlocks the Setnayan broadcaster UI's multi-cam switching for that day; without it a Daily Broadcast is single-cam). **(3) Annual Streaming** ₱2,999/year (single-cam unlimited days for one year — vendor-friendly for vendors who livestream regularly to their own YouTube). **(4) Annual Streaming Plus** ₱3,999/year (multi-cam unlimited days for one year). **Retired from prior spec:** `live_stream_base` ₱2,499 + `live_stream_camera_addon` ₱999 + `live_stream_hour_addon` ₱999 + `broadcast_style_pack` ₱2,999 — all features that depended on Cloudflare-composite (lower-thirds, scene cards, 4-mode style switching, ffmpeg compositor overlays) are no longer available because the composite step is gone. Couples wanting the old style-pack experience use YouTube's own built-in production tools or third-party OBS-style apps writing to their YouTube. **Architecture impact:** Setnayan iteration 0011 becomes a **thin broadcaster orchestration layer** (multi-cam phone client connecting to YouTube via the couple's OAuth + landing-page IFrame embed of the couple's YouTube Live URL) rather than a media compositor. Custom Monogram Pack (₱1,999) still applies for landing-page chrome but no longer touches the broadcast video itself (couple sets their own YouTube channel branding). Same-Day Edit (₱24,999) SKU dependency on Cloudflare-Stream-recorded feeds is severed; SDE now reads from the couple's YouTube archive via OAuth + Papic photo stream — engineering re-scope needed at V1.5+ SDE build time. AI Video Highlight (₱999/60s) and AI Edited Highlight (₱2,999/3min) similarly consume the couple's YouTube archive. **Day-of-build engineering surface drops by ~60%** — no Cloudflare Stream Live ingest, no SFU subscription, no server-side ffmpeg compositor with monogram overlay, no RTMP relay to a master Setnayan channel; broadcaster web UI + landing-page IFrame embed are the entire V1 build. | Three drivers. **First**, composite costs were the largest variable-cost line in the Panood economics: Cloudflare Stream Live ingest at ~$1 per 1,000 minutes per camera (5 cams × 5 hrs × 60min = 1,500 minutes × ~₱60 = ~₱90 per typical event), plus server-side ffmpeg compositor compute, plus RTMP relay. Pushing the composite to YouTube (where it is free at unbounded scale) and shifting Setnayan's role to broadcaster orchestration drops the variable cost line to near zero. **Second**, the couple-owns-the-video model resolves a long-standing tension around "what happens when Setnayan eventually wraps or rebrands or rotates the @SetnayanWeddings channel?" — by storing the video on the couple's own YouTube, the broadcast is durable independent of Setnayan's platform lifecycle. **Third**, per-day pricing aligns with how couples actually plan multi-day Filipino weddings (prep day + ceremony + reception are often 3 distinct days at distinct venues); buying coverage day-by-day is more honest than a 3-hour base + hour-addons model that mismatches a 2-day or 3-day event. The Annual SKUs (₱2,999 / ₱3,999) open a vendor-side ARR line — vendors who livestream their own portfolio events year-round have a single-purchase option that's break-even after ~6 days/year of use. **Tax-tier note:** Daily Broadcast nets ~67-72% margin under V1 tax tier; Annual SKUs net ~70-72% (higher because COGS is amortized across many broadcasts per year). | `CLAUDE.md` decision log (this entry); `0011_panood/0011_panood.md` (Pricing section — base + add-ons table rewritten to the 4 new SKUs: Daily Broadcast ₱499/day, Camera Sync ₱99/day, Annual Streaming ₱2,999/year, Annual Streaming Plus ₱3,999/year · Cloudflare-composite SKUs `live_stream_base` + `live_stream_camera_addon` + `live_stream_hour_addon` + `broadcast_style_pack` marked RETIRED · "Delivery architecture" section rewritten from Cloudflare Stream Live + ffmpeg compositor + master channel to BYO YouTube via OAuth · Pipeline subsection retired · Setnayan's master YouTube channel subsection retired · Embed implementation simplified to IFrame embed of couple's YouTube Live URL · Pro Camera Bridge cross-iteration reference to 0012 preserved · SDE engineering re-scope flagged at V1.5+); | 2026-05-16 | **Save-the-Date Video SKU ₱99/render reintroduced as a downloadable MP4 product · distinct from the retired ₱99 Save-the-Date Render SKU · drives traffic to the free Phase 1 landing page.** Fifth 2026-05-16 row. **Reintroduces** a Save-the-Date Video product at ₱99/render, but **explicitly distinguishes it from the retired `save_the_date_render` SKU** killed in the first 2026-05-16 row of this day. The retired SKU was a multi-aspect-ratio composite of the couple's landing-page hero (3 outputs: 16:9 + 1:1 + 9:16) rendered from the page's animated SVG monogram + countdown — that whole pipeline is gone. **This is a different product:** a **generic-template AI-auto-edit short MP4** generated from **5-10 engagement photos** uploaded by the couple, scored with **Setnayan-owned music** from the AI catalogue, output as a single polished **30-60 second vertical MP4** sized for social sharing (IG Reels, TikTok, FB stories). Couple downloads the MP4 directly; share-flow nudges them to also share the **free landing-page URL** at the end of the MP4 (closing 2-second card with `setnayan.com/[couple-slug]`) so every social share drives traffic back to the free landing page. **Input:** 5-10 engagement photos uploaded via the Setnayan upload widget (per-photo basic validation: ≤5MB, JPG/PNG, ≥1200×1200 recommended). **Template:** 8-12 generic templates in V1 (modern minimalist, romantic, vintage, cinematic, fun, etc.) selected at purchase time; templates are FFmpeg compositions with Lottie overlays for animated text — no per-couple custom design. **AI auto-edit:** scene-ordering heuristic (faces detected · landscape vs portrait crop · color-palette match) selects the per-photo order automatically; couple does not manually sequence. **Music:** Setnayan-owned AI catalogue (~400 tracks); couple picks category at purchase (Bridgerton / Pop / Hip-hop / Jazz / Acoustic / Cinematic). **Output:** single 30-60s 1080×1920 vertical MP4 (H.264, no watermark), downloadable from couple dashboard within ~5 minutes of upload completion. **SKU:** `save_the_date_video_render` ₱99 / one render (multi-purchase if couple wants multiple variants — e.g. one for IG, one for TikTok with different music). **Naming clarity:** the new SKU code `save_the_date_video_render` is **deliberately different** from the retired `save_the_date_render` SKU code to keep the audit trail clean (the retired SKU never shipped; if it had, OR voids / refunds would need to keep the old code distinct). | Three drivers. **First**, the free landing-page Phase 1 hero (locked first 2026-05-16 row) covers the *guest-facing* job-to-be-done (couple shares a link, guests open and save the date) but does not cover the *couple's own social-feed* job-to-be-done — couples still want a short, polished video to post on their personal IG / TikTok feed announcing the engagement. A 30-60s MP4 generated from engagement photos with Setnayan-owned music + closing-card-link to the landing page solves that job *and* doubles as marketing surface for the free landing page (every social share is a Setnayan-branded MP4 with a `setnayan.com/[couple-slug]` end-card driving traffic back to the platform). **Second**, the ₱99 price point is intentionally a low-friction social-share upsell, not a margin product — Setnayan's break-even is ~₱5-10 per render (FFmpeg compute on Cloudflare Workers + R2 storage + Setnayan-owned music = ~₱0 licensing cost), so the SKU still nets ~85-90% gross margin and ~70% net margin under V1 tax tier. The volume play is what matters: at a ₱99 price point and 30% attach rate on the 1,000-event V1 cohort, that is ~₱30K/mo in pure-funnel revenue *plus* every share is a Setnayan marketing surface. **Third**, distinguishing it from the retired SKU as a *different product* (different SKU code, different input model, different output model) keeps the audit trail clean. The retired SKU was a "render the landing-page hero into 3 video aspect ratios" feature; this is "AI-edit 5-10 engagement photos into one social-share clip" — fundamentally different inputs, fundamentally different outputs, different engineering pipelines. The naming distinction matters for OR / refund / audit / SKU history hygiene. | `CLAUDE.md` decision log (this entry); `0024_save_the_date/0024_save_the_date.md` (new § "Save-the-Date Video SKU ₱99 — reintroduced 2026-05-16 (separate product)" inserted after the retired-SKU table · explicitly distinguishes the new product from the retired one · documents inputs / templates / AI auto-edit / music / output / SKU code · preserves the existing page-reframe content above it — the free landing-page Phase 1 hero is NOT undone, this is an additive standalone MP4 product); `0034_payments_and_cart/0034_payments_and_cart.md` (`service_catalog` seed: add `save_the_date_video_render` 9900 row, category `save_the_date_video`, is_multi_purchase TRUE · retired `save_the_date_render` row left in place as an audit row but with comment "retired 2026-05-16 - replaced by save_the_date_video_render with different scope"); `API_Integration_Checklist.md` (Tier 5.2 FFmpeg render pipeline row appended with Save-the-Date Video render queue note · new `std-video-render-queue` Cloudflare Queue + Worker reading from R2 `setnayan-media/std-video-uploads/` and writing to `setnayan-media/std-video-renders/`); `App_Build_Status.md` (0024 row note updated to reflect that ₱99 MP4 SKU is back as a distinct product); `V1_Gap_Analysis_Status.md` (0024 row updated). **`.docx` mirrors NOT regenerated** (pandoc unavailable). **Engineering implementation pending** — upload widget for 5-10 engagement photos in the couple's add-ons flow, template picker UI (8-12 templates), music category picker, FFmpeg + Lottie render Worker on Cloudflare with R2 routing, 5-minute render SLA wiring, MP4 download surface on couple dashboard with "share this MP4" nudge that includes the landing-page URL end-card overlay. **Marketplace commission row INTENTIONALLY EXCLUDED from this commit batch.** **Sequencing note:** Fifth 2026-05-16 row. |
| 2026-05-16 | **Patiktok V1 SKU lock — dual-tier (Setnayan TikTok ₱999/day vs Personal TikTok ₱1,999/day) · 40-video soft cap per booth per day · ₱49/+10 overage · per-day multi-purchase.** Sixth 2026-05-16 row. Patiktok pricing model **replaces** the prior single-SKU ₱2,499/booth/5hr model (and its ₱999 additional-station + ₱499/hour add-on tier) with a **dual-tier per-day** model based on **who owns the videos**. **(1) Setnayan TikTok tier — ₱999/day:** videos auto-post to **Setnayan's master TikTok handle `@SetnayanWeddings`** (or similar); Setnayan retains ad-revenue upside if the compilation goes viral; couple gets the post link + downloadable MP4 with Setnayan-owned music. Same posting flow as the prior single-SKU spec. **(2) Personal TikTok tier — ₱1,999/day:** **couple BYO TikTok via OAuth** (one-time OAuth handshake during purchase flow); videos auto-post to the couple's own TikTok handle; couple owns all videos + analytics + ad-revenue upside. **(3) Soft cap: 40 videos per day per booth** — protects Setnayan margin (compilation render + storage + per-clip face-lock processing scales with video count); booth dashboard shows a live counter; at 40 the operator sees a soft-warning ("You've captured your day's allotted 40 videos · keep recording with the overage add-on") and can either stop or buy overage. **(4) Overage SKU: ₱49 per +10 videos** (multi-purchase — operator can stack as many +10 blocks as they want at the venue without leaving the booth flow). **(5) Per-day multi-purchase for multi-day events** — Filipino weddings often span 2-3 days (prep + ceremony + reception each at a different venue); couple buys per-day Patiktok exactly like Panood Daily Broadcast (₱999 × 3 = ₱2,997 for the Setnayan-tier 3-day, ₱1,999 × 3 = ₱5,997 for the Personal-tier 3-day). **Sound selection mechanics from the prior spec preserved:** couple curates 2 trending sounds (primary + backup) at purchase time; printable QR for the operator dashboard; multi-performer face-lock; downloadable backup copy with Setnayan-owned music (for off-TikTok sharing). **External display + dual-view UX preserved** (split-screen / PIP for venues with monitors). | Three drivers. **First**, the prior single-SKU ₱2,499/booth/5hr model under-served couples with multi-day weddings (a 3-day event meant either buying multiple full stations or skipping the booth on most days) and over-served couples with single-event-day weddings (5 hours is more than most receptions need). Per-day pricing matches event reality and the per-day Panood pattern decided in the same session. **Second**, the dual-tier split by video-ownership resolves a long-standing tension in the original spec — some couples want the viral marketing upside of `@SetnayanWeddings` (Setnayan amplifies their wedding to the platform's audience for free), other couples want their own TikTok to be where the wedding content lives forever (and want the ad-revenue + analytics). Charging differently for these two ownership models reflects the real value difference: BYO TikTok means Setnayan loses platform-marketing upside, so the price is ~2× to compensate. **Third**, the 40-video soft cap is calibrated to typical Filipino-wedding guest counts (200 guests × ~20% participation rate ≈ 40 unique submitters per booth per day); the soft cap rather than a hard cap with ₱49/+10 overage protects margin on outlier high-engagement events without forcing couples to buy a whole second booth purchase. The ₱49 overage charm-pricing keeps the in-event upsell low-friction. **Tax-tier note:** Setnayan-tier ₱999/day nets ~70% margin under V1 tax tier; Personal-tier ₱1,999/day nets ~72% (higher % because the OAuth + per-couple TikTok adds ~₱0 marginal cost vs the Setnayan-handle posting); overage SKU at ₱49 nets ~80%. | `CLAUDE.md` decision log (this entry); `0017_patiktok/0017_patiktok.md` (§ Pricing rewritten — old ₱2,499/booth/5hr table retired · new dual-tier per-day table inserted with the 4 SKU rows above · TikTok integration § rewritten to describe **two posting paths**: Setnayan-tier auto-post to `@SetnayanWeddings` (preserved from old spec) + Personal-tier OAuth-based auto-post to couple's own handle (new section) · sound-selection / multi-performer / external-display / downloadable-backup subsections preserved · soft-cap + overage subsection added · Coordinator workflow section updated to reference per-day multi-purchase · Anti-abuse rules table updated — the prior 500-submission-per-station-per-event cap is replaced by the 40-videos/day soft cap + overage); | 2026-05-16 | **V1 blended net margin lock at V1 tax tier — ~67-72% net across most SKUs · 90% gross margin (COGS ≤10%) achieved · 90% NET mathematically impossible under PH tax law · projected ~₱4M annual net profit at 1,000 events × ₱6K avg revenue.** Seventh 2026-05-16 row. Closes today's V1 SKU lock burst with a margin-discipline lock to prevent future scope drift toward "90% net margin" framing that's mathematically impossible under PH non-VAT V1 tax. **(1) V1 tax assumption locked:** Percentage Tax 3% (NIRC § 116 · annual gross ≤₱3M threshold) + Local Business Tax 1% (LBT — Manila / Makati rate) + Income Tax 25% (graduated table corporate rate post first ₱5M). Total tax wedge ~28-29% of gross revenue. **(2) Achievable net margin range:** ~67-72% across most V1 SKUs. **(3) Achievable gross margin range:** **~90% (COGS ≤10%)** — this is the "90% margin" headline that's accurate when properly labeled as **gross**, not net. **(4) Why 90% NET is impossible:** PH non-VAT tax wedge (~28-29%) + non-zero COGS (storage / compute / SMS / OAuth-API quotas) puts the theoretical max net margin at ~72% even with 100% gross margin SKUs. The headline "90% margin" claim only holds at gross. **(5) Annual net profit projection at V1 scale:** 1,000 events × ₱6,000 avg revenue per event = **₱6M annual gross**; minus 10% COGS = ₱5.4M gross profit; minus 28% tax wedge = **~₱4M annual net profit**. **(6) Worst-case tax tier (V1.5+ when annual gross crosses ₱3M VAT-registration threshold):** 12% VAT + 35% income tax (top bracket) puts the wedge at ~42-45%; net margin floats to ~52-57% across SKUs. **All SKUs remain profitable** even at worst-case tax tier — no V1 SKU is below break-even under V2 tax regime, so the upgrade path does not force re-pricing. **(7) Per-SKU net-margin snapshot at V1 tax tier:** Save-the-Date Video ₱99 = ~70% net · Monogram Hero ₱1,999 = ~70% net (Potrace ~₱0 cost / minimal R2 storage) · Live Schedule ₱999 = ~71% net · Panood Daily Broadcast ₱499 = ~67-70% net (broadcaster compute) · Panood Camera Sync ₱99/day = ~70% net · Panood Annual ₱2,999 = ~70-72% net · Panood Annual Plus ₱3,999 = ~70-72% net · Patiktok Setnayan ₱999/day = ~70% net · Patiktok Personal ₱1,999/day = ~72% net · Patiktok overage ₱49/+10 = ~80% net · all V1.5+ Papic SKUs land in the 65-72% net band per row 3 above. **(8) Disciplined revenue framing rule:** internal docs + investor materials + marketing copy must label margin claims explicitly as "gross" or "net"; the bare "90% margin" headline without qualifier is **retired** from V1 messaging because it conflates the two and creates expectation-management debt. | Three drivers. **First**, the V1 tax tier (non-VAT · ₱3M-gross threshold · 3% Percentage Tax) is a deliberate choice the corporate filing has committed to, not a stretch assumption — but it sets a mathematical ceiling on net margin that is lower than the colloquial "90% margin" framing in pre-launch decks would suggest. Locking the assumption now (rather than discovering it during BIR Form 1701Q quarterly filing) lets the revenue model + investor narrative be honest from launch. **Second**, locking the per-SKU net-margin snapshot at the V1 tax tier with the 5 SKU locks already decided today (Papic V1.5+ pricing · Panood per-day · Save-the-Date Video · Patiktok dual-tier) consolidates today's decision burst into one verifiable economic story — every SKU lock today rolls up to the ₱4M annual net projection at 1,000 events. The projection is a back-of-envelope but it is traceable to today's specific lock decisions, not aspirational marketing. **Third**, calling out the worst-case V2 tax tier (12% VAT + 35% income at the top corporate bracket) and showing the model is still profitable under that regime — net floats to 52-57% — locks in that V1 SKU prices do NOT need to be revised when Setnayan crosses the VAT-registration threshold. Owner-ratified design target finalized — **3% net to Setnayan after all taxes at worst-case tax tier**. **(1) Math:** required gross = 3% ÷ (1 − tax_wedge) → V1 small-biz 28% wedge needs 4.17% gross · V2 VAT-registered 35% wedge needs 4.62% gross · extreme 40% wedge needs 5.00% gross. **5.0% flat is the minimum gross that holds the 3% net floor under every plausible tax scenario** with cushion for chargebacks / failed transactions / disbursement-fee absorption. **(2) Yields by tier at 5.0% flat:** V1 (28% wedge) → 3.60% net (1.67× the 2.16% operating breakeven); V2 realistic (35% wedge) → 3.25% net (1.50×); extreme worst (40% wedge) → 3.00% net (1.39×). **(3) Option B (vendor-absorbs-gateway) confirmed** over Option A (Setnayan-absorbs-gateway) because (a) Stripe Connect / Airbnb / Lazada Marketplace / every PH marketplace works this way so vendors expect it · (b) it insulates Setnayan from gateway rate risk forever (if Maya raises QR Ph from 1.5% → 2%, vendor absorbs not Setnayan) · (c) it lets the customer-facing headline stay at a clean flat 5.0% without rail-specific math at the cart · (d) Vendor Studio subscribers can be offered a gateway-absorbed perk in V1.5 as a subscription-conversion lever without disturbing V1 economics. | 2026-05-17 | **V1.5+ vendor disbursement automation locked via Maya Business Bulk Fund Transfer — three-rail routing (Intra-Maya instant+free · InstaPay <1min+₱10 absorbed · PESONet EOD+₱15 absorbed) · default rail per payout type · vendor override in 0022 with ₱5 rebate-for-downgrade / pay-for-upgrade pricing · Maya Bank vendor-recruiting copy added to 0006 Vendor Payout model + 0022 onboarding tour + verification approval email · new `disbursement_batches` table + `vendor_payouts.{rail, rail_chosen_by, batch_id, status}` columns in 0034 § 6.9 schema.** First 2026-05-17 row. Adds the outbound-disbursement half of the marketplace payment architecture, complementing the inbound Setnayan Pay flow locked yesterday (rows 16-17 of 2026-05-16). **(1) Three rails, three speeds, three costs:** **Intra-Maya** (vendor has Maya Bank account → instant + free + 24/7 for both vendor and Setnayan); **InstaPay** (Maya → any PH bank → < 1 min + 24/7 incl. weekends + ~₱10 bulk rate absorbed by Setnayan); **PESONet** (Maya → any PH bank → EOD same banking day (or T+1 weekends/holidays) + ~₱15 bulk rate absorbed by Setnayan). **(2) Default routing per payout type:** verified vendor immediate payout → InstaPay; coming_soon vendor 3-stage milestone → PESONet; any vendor on Maya Bank → intra-Maya regardless of payout type; payouts < ₱500 or > ₱500K (above InstaPay cap) → PESONet. **(3) Vendor override** in 0022 Vendor Dashboard payout preferences — verified vendors can downgrade default to PESONet for ₱5/payout rebate credit (Setnayan saves ₱5, vendor earns ₱5, both incentivized); coming_soon vendors can upgrade individual milestone to InstaPay by absorbing the ₱5 difference. **(4) Maya Bank vendor-recruiting pitch** — canonical copy "Get paid instantly, free, 24/7 — open a Maya Bank business account · Or get paid in under a minute to any PH bank, including weekends (InstaPay) · Standard payout settles end of business day (PESONet) — default for milestone releases." Surfaces on verification approval email + 0022 onboarding tour + payout-preferences settings. Strongest vendor-recruiting incentive in the payments architecture — every Maya Bank account opened means instant+free payouts for the vendor AND zero disbursement cost for Setnayan, forever. **(5) Schema (0034 § 6.9):** new `disbursement_batches` table (batch_id · generated_by_admin_id · rail enum (instapay/pesonet/mixed) · csv_r2_key · recipient_count · total_centavos · status enum (pending_upload/uploaded/partial_success/complete/failed) · maya_batch_reference · row_outcomes JSONB · timestamps); new columns on `vendor_payouts` (`rail` enum, `rail_chosen_by` enum, `batch_id` FK nullable, `status` enum widened to pending/batched/disbursed/failed/manual_reconciliation); two new indexes for batch-status queries. **(6) Failure handling:** if Maya rejects any row in a bulk batch (invalid account number, KYC mismatch, frozen account), that payout's status reverts to `pending` and rejoins next-day batch. Partial-success batches log per-row outcomes in `disbursement_batches.row_outcomes`. Three consecutive batch failures for same vendor trigger admin alert + automatic move to manual reconciliation for that vendor until they update their disbursement details. **(7) Annual disbursement cost absorbed by Setnayan (planning assumption, reconciles to actual Maya quote once business account is approved):** ~₱2,500/yr at 200 couples · ~₱6,500/yr at 500 couples · ~₱13K/yr at 1,000 couples · ~₱65K/yr at 5,000 couples — every scenario stays under 0.3% of platform revenue. **(8) Operational efficiency unlock (the real value):** per-payout admin time collapses from ~5 minutes (manual click-through) to ~5 seconds (one CSV row in daily batch upload). At 500 couples = ~37 hours/yr saved; at 5,000 couples = ~370 hours/yr saved. Admin headcount doesn't grow proportionally with booking volume. | Three drivers. **First, vendor payouts at scale require batching automation that the current V1 manual reconciliation flow does not provide.** The manual flow is acceptable for V1 (low booking volume, single admin) but breaks operationally at ~50+ payouts/week. Maya Business Bulk Fund Transfer (the user-shared product page lock) is the cleanest fit because (a) it sits on top of the same Maya Business merchant account that V1.5+ inbound Setnayan Pay already requires, (b) it routes through BSP's standard InstaPay + PESONet rails so vendors receive money via the rails they already trust, and (c) the bulk CSV upload pattern fits Setnayan's daily-batch admin cadence without requiring a real-time disbursement API. **Second, the three-rail routing isn't arbitrary** — each rail maps to a specific BSP-defined cost/speed trade-off (InstaPay = sub-minute real-time gross settlement; PESONet = end-of-day batch settlement; intra-Maya = zero-cost internal book transfer). The default routing rules (verified→InstaPay, coming_soon→PESONet, Maya-Bank→intra) optimize for what each vendor segment actually wants: verified vendors want speed (Setnayan absorbs the ₱10 to keep them happy); coming_soon vendors haven't earned speed yet (PESONet is the right default + saves Setnayan ₱5/payout); Maya Bank vendors are the strictly-best outcome for everyone. **Third, the Maya Bank vendor-recruiting copy is genuinely aligned, not promotional** — every Maya Bank account opened means an instant+free payout experience for the vendor AND a zero-fee payout cost for Setnayan, forever. This is the rare case where the marketing pitch and the platform economics point the same direction without any compromise. Vendors who don't switch to Maya Bank still get fully functional payouts (InstaPay/PESONet); Setnayan still absorbs their disbursement cost; nobody loses. But the more vendors who do switch, the better the marketplace economics get for everyone. **Pricing note:** Maya Business does not publish Bulk Fund Transfer pricing publicly — quote-based per business based on monthly volume commitment. Locked numbers (~₱10 InstaPay / ~₱15 PESONet) are V1.5+ planning assumptions derived from (a) Maya's published individual rates (₱15 InstaPay outbound · ₱15-25 PESONet outbound) and (b) industry-standard 30-40% bulk discount;
