Try 3 days free →" link below picker, hidden when `users.concierge_trial_used_at IS NOT NULL` OR `users.concierge_enforcement_level IN ('trial_banned', 'full_banned')`. **(10) Settings tab (iteration 0025):** picker collapses to single-Concierge option · 3-day trial CTA gated by account-level state · new "Enforcement state" surface for warning / trial_banned / full_banned states with appeal-ticket CTA · "Trial used" empty-state when `concierge_trial_used_at IS NOT NULL` (couple has used their one trial). **(11) Dashboard variants (iteration 0021 § 2.0b):** 4-state model preserved (DIY · Trial · Active · Expired) but Trial copy updated from 7-day to 3-day; banner CTAs collapse to single "Continue with Concierge (₱4,999)" button (no Essentials option). Banned account variant shows the explanatory copy + appeal CTA in place of the upgrade banner. | Two drivers. **First, single-SKU = product confidence.** The 2026-05-16 2-tier model still read as a SaaS discount ladder ("we have a cheap option and a real option") rather than a confident product posture ("here's the product · ₱4,999"). The Apple iPhone playbook (one price per model · optional accessories not optional tiers) lands better in the wedding category where couples spend ₱200K–2M on the event itself — Setnayan looks more like a category-defining product and less like a subscription menu. The ₱2,499 Essentials tier was projected to under-perform vs Complete anyway (the savings math at ₱500/6-month-extra didn't anchor; most converters were projected to pick Complete), so retiring it removes a low-conversion SKU + simplifies the marketing surface + removes a "save face" branch that some couples were going to pick for budget reasons rather than fit reasons. Net revenue per Concierge customer is now uniformly ₱4,999 (was bimodal ₱2,499/₱4,999), which simplifies internal forecasting + makes the pricing-page anchor (₱25K coordinator vs ₱4,999 Concierge) cleaner without the ₱2,499 mid-anchor cluttering the comparison. **Second, the 3-day trial + account-level cap + tiered enforcement framework closes a real multi-account abuse vector** the owner identified. The 2026-05-16 7-day per-event preview model had two known holes: (a) one couple creating Event A, exhausting trial, creating Event B on the same account for another trial; (b) one person creating Account A, exhausting trial, creating Account B with a near-identical wedding profile for another trial. Hole (a) closes mechanically with the per-account cap (`users.concierge_trial_used_at`). Hole (b) requires similarity detection — the on-trial-start check + admin review queue + tiered enforcement framework. The tiered enforcement (warn → trial-ban → full-ban) is more forgiving than a single-strike auto-ban because (i) similarity hits include genuine false positives (sibling couples planning at the same venue · wedding-planner accounts managing multiple clients · same venue different couples on different dates) which need admin judgment, and (ii) the progressive penalty creates a forgiveness lane on first offense that reduces customer-support load from legit users wrongly hit on the first flag. Filipino-market consideration: wedding-coordinator accounts and multi-client agencies are a legit segment that will pattern-match on venue/date overlap with their own clients — these are NOT abuse and need admin-confirmable clearing on first flag. The tiered model gives the platform room to learn without permanently banning legitimate edge cases. **Trial duration 7 → 3 days drivers:** (a) 3 days is enough to walk through the 9-step roadmap and see the Concierge value (each step is ~5-10 minutes for an engaged couple); (b) shorter trial reduces account-creation incentive for trial-cycling (3 days of free access is less "worth the abuse effort" than 7 days); (c) the ₱4,999 sticker is now anchored against "a focused 72-hour preview" rather than "a leisurely week" — better matches the premium-product feel that supports the single-SKU framing. **Risk accepted:** lower trial → buy conversion than the 7-day model would have produced. Mitigated by (i) the 9-step roadmap being demonstrably valuable in the first hour (couples see deadline alerts + vendor picks within Step 1-2), (ii) the choice card still offering DIY-free as the no-cost option for couples who aren't ready, (iii) the human-coordinator anchor still doing the heavy lifting on pricing-page conversion. | `CLAUDE.md` decision log (this entry) · iteration table row #0016 (rewritten to single-SKU + 3-day trial + tiered enforcement framing); | 2026-05-17 | **Setnayan Concierge access switched from fixed-12-months to wedding-anchored with a 24-month cap — fixes the long-engagement edge case where a couple with a 3-year engagement was losing access 24 months before their wedding day.** Third 2026-05-17 row. Owner-surfaced edge-case fix: under the prior fixed-12-month spec, a couple setting their wedding 3 years out and paying ₱4,999 would have lost Concierge 24 months before they actually needed it — a bad customer experience that risked refund disputes and brand damage. **(1) New access-duration formula:** `concierge_expires_at = LEAST(GREATEST(wedding_date + INTERVAL '30 days', activation_date + INTERVAL '12 months'), activation_date + INTERVAL '24 months')`. **(2) Guarantees:** every paying couple gets a **floor of 12 months** of access from activation (so couples with no date yet OR very-soon weddings still get a full year), and a **ceiling of 24 months** from activation (caps margin exposure on extreme long engagements). **(3) Sweet-spot ranges:** wedding 3 months out → 12 months access (12-month floor wins · 9 months post-wedding tail) · wedding 8 months out → 12 months (floor wins) · wedding 12 months out → 12.5 months (wedding+30 wins) · wedding 18 months out → 18.5 months (wedding+30) · wedding 24 months out → 24 months (cap) · wedding 36 months out → 24 months (cap · couple sees 24-month advisory). **(4) NULL wedding_date handling:** at activation, if `events.wedding_date IS NULL` (typical because the choice card per 0000 § 2.5a defers date entry to Concierge Step 1 OR Profile), `expires_at` defaults to `activation_date + INTERVAL '12 months'`. When `wedding_date` is later set/updated, expires_at recomputes per the formula above — but **only extends, never shrinks**. **(5) Wedding-date update behavior:** if couple updates `wedding_date` to a later date after activation, `concierge_expires_at` extends to the new wedding+30 (up to the 24-month cap). If couple updates to an earlier date, expires_at STAYS at the original value (they already paid for that runway; no shrinkage). **(6) Long-engagement advisory:** when `wedding_date` is set or updated to > 24 months from `concierge_activated_at`, a one-time in-app + email advisory surfaces: *"Your wedding is more than 24 months away. Setnayan Concierge covers up to 24 months from your purchase date — you'll lose access ~{N} months before your wedding. We recommend renewing closer to your wedding for full coverage."* Stamp a `concierge_long_engagement_advised_at TIMESTAMPTZ` column on `events` to prevent re-fire on subsequent date updates. **(7) Schema:** the existing `events.concierge_expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ` column from the 2026-05-17 lock is unchanged structurally — just the formula that populates it changes; new column `events.concierge_long_engagement_advised_at TIMESTAMPTZ` added for the advisory de-dup. **(8) Server-action update:** `activate_concierge(event_id, order_id)` computes `expires_at` per the formula at activation time using whatever `wedding_date` value is present (NULL → defaults to activation+12mo). New server action `recompute_concierge_expiry(event_id)` fires from the `events.wedding_date` update trigger (or app-layer hook) — recomputes per the formula + applies the extend-only rule + triggers the advisory if conditions met. **(9) Daily expiry sweep unchanged** — still flips status to `'expired'` when `expires_at < NOW()`. **(10) Refund/dispute exposure capped** — under the prior model, a couple paying ₱4,999 with a 36-month engagement and losing access at month 12 had a strong "I was misled" case; under the new model the worst-case is a couple with a >24-month engagement, and they see the advisory at purchase/date-entry, so they make an informed choice. | Two drivers. **First, the prior fixed-12-months model created a real product-market mismatch for long engagements.** Filipino couples plan 6–24 months out modally (per the locked planning-runway assumptions in iteration 0016 § 1), but a non-trivial tail (anniversary-fresh engagements · couples who got engaged years before they could afford the wedding · couples coordinating with overseas family that need long lead times) plans 24–48 months out. Under the prior model these couples paid ₱4,999 and lost access well before the wedding — the value proposition collapsed precisely when it mattered most. The wedding-anchored formula matches the actual job-to-be-done ("help us plan THIS wedding") without breaking the simple single-SKU pricing model. **Second, the 24-month cap protects Setnayan's per-event economics.** A truly unbounded wedding-anchored model (e.g., access until wedding_date + 30 days with no cap) would mean a 5-year-engagement couple gets 5 years of Concierge for ₱4,999 — that's an effective rate of ₱83/month, well below the per-customer economics this SKU was sized for (~₱416/month over 12 months). Capping at 24 months means the worst-case effective rate is ~₱208/month, still healthy margin, and the affected customer segment (>24-month engagements) is small. The advisory + renewal-encouragement copy turns the cap from a hidden gotcha into a transparent renewal hook. **Third, the 12-month floor protects the short-engagement / no-date-yet case** — couples who buy Concierge before setting a wedding date OR with very-soon weddings still get a guaranteed full year of access including post-wedding planning tail, matching the brand promise that "Access doesn't end at the wedding date." **Filipino-market consideration:** the long-engagement-advisory copy will be in EN-primary luxurious-Filipino-modern voice (per COWORK.md line 74) and will not penalize couples who got engaged years in advance — it surfaces as a friendly "heads-up" not a "you bought wrong" guilt-trip. **Extend-only rule on date changes** is the customer-fair default — a couple who postpones their wedding deserves more runway; a couple who moves it earlier already paid for the longer runway and gets to keep it (no surprise shrinkage). | `CLAUDE.md` decision log (this entry) · iteration table row #0016 (rewritten to reflect wedding-anchored access + 24-month cap framing); | 2026-05-17 | **Setnayan Pay convenience fee minimum floor locked at ₱50 — extends the flat 5.0% lock with a per-booking floor.** Formula at checkout: `fees_centavos = MAX(subtotal_centavos × setnayan_fee_bps / 10000, min_fee_centavos)` where `min_fee_centavos = 5000` (₱50) is the default in `payment_method_config` per 0023 § 3.5d (admin-configurable per method · single-admin-authority + audit-log pattern matches the rate column). **Activates only below ₱1,000 vendor booking** (the 5%-meets-₱50 crossover); 99%+ of wedding-vendor bookings are unaffected. Affects mostly small supply purchases / micro add-ons in the supplies marketplace. **Customer-facing copy** (cart drawer · marketing site · vendor agreement): *"Setnayan Pay convenience fee — 5% per booking, ₱50 minimum."* **Vendor opt-in interaction (per 0034 § 6.8):** if vendor absorbs the convenience fee on a small booking, ₱50 floor still applies to vendor — floor protects Setnayan's per-transaction operating cost regardless of which side pays. **Worked example at the floor:** ₱500 vendor item → ₱50 floor (5% × ₱500 = ₱25, floor wins) → customer pays ₱550 total. Crossover at exactly ₱1,000 booking. **Schema migration** (V1 deployable): `ALTER TABLE payment_method_config ADD COLUMN min_fee_centavos INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 5000`. | Owner pick: ₱50 over ₱150/₱200 alternatives I proposed. Economic trade-off accepted: ₱50 × 72% (V1 28% tax wedge) = ₱36 net per small booking — below the V1 ₱80-130 operating cost band (admin time + disbursement absorption), so Setnayan loses ~₱50-90 on each booking below ₱1,000 in V1. But sub-₱1K vendor bookings are rare in the wedding category (1-2% of all bookings; supplies/micro-add-ons only); aggregate annual loss is ~₱720 at 200 couples → ~₱3,600 at 1,000 couples — negligible against platform revenue (rounding error against ~₱14M+ at 1K-couple scale). V1.5+ rebalances cleanly: Maya Bulk Fund Transfer drops admin cost to ₱30-50, so ₱36 net at the floor moves to roughly breakeven. ₱50 also anchors close to PH payment-processor flat-fee norms (PayMongo ₱5-15 · Stripe ~₱17 equivalent · GCash transfer ₱15) — feels fair to customers; the ₱150 alternative I proposed would have felt punitive on small purchases ("30% effective on a ₱500 booking" reads worse than "10% on a ₱500 booking" even though both clear Setnayan's break-even at scale). **Customer-experience priority** over per-booking margin discipline on the rare small-booking case. | `0034_payments_and_cart/0034_payments_and_cart.md` § 6.1 cart math — added Minimum fee floor paragraph + worked example for a ₱500 booking at the floor + crossover-point note + vendor opt-in interaction + customer-facing copy block; | 2026-05-17 | **App Store-style add-on detail surface — Panood pilot shipped; shared layout will fan out to other 8 add-ons + vendor service detail.** Owner directive: when a couple opens an individual add-on from the Add-ons bottom-nav (Panood as the worked example), the detail screen should mirror the iOS App Store listing: hero with icon + tagline + price-from + Choose Plan CTA, horizontal stat carousel (rating · purchases · % events use it · price-from), Preview screenshot rail, Sample outputs rail, About-this-feature description + Plans & pricing table, Ratings & Reviews ▸ deep-link, Event Privacy, Data Linked to You, Accessibility. **Same template applies to vendor service detail** when a couple opens an individual service from a vendor's profile (planned fan-out after the Panood pilot validates). **Architecture decisions:** (1) The previous `panood/page.tsx` (986 lines of post-purchase OAuth + broadcaster setup) is the *owner* surface and moves to `panood/setup/page.tsx`; the new `panood/page.tsx` is the *discovery* surface; the App Store hero CTA flips by ownership — not-owned shows **Choose plan · from ₱499/day** opening a bottom-sheet (mobile) / right-drawer (desktop) of all 7 Panood SKUs, owned shows **Open Panood setup** linking to `/setup`. (2) Shared layout components live at `apps/web/app/_components/app-store/{layout.tsx, choose-plan-sheet.tsx}` — content-agnostic so vendor service detail can mount the same component with different data. (3) New `public.feature_reviews` table (sibling of `vendor_reviews`) — one row per (feature_key, event_id, couple_user_id), public read + couple-only write tied to `current_couple_event_ids()`; writes are gated post-event in the app layer; surfaced on `/dashboard/[eventId]/add-ons/panood/reviews`. (4) Stat carousel reads live from `orders` + `feature_reviews` + `events` via `apps/web/lib/add-on-stats.ts`; below thresholds (orders < 5 AND reviews < 3) the layout renders a "Just launched · early access" chip per the launch-honesty rule. (5) Plans table + Choose-plan sheet drive every row off the V1 SKU lock (`service_catalog`), formatted via `formatPhp()` from `lib/orders.ts` — PHP only, no token display (token wallet was retired 2026-05-11). Add-to-cart deep-links to `/dashboard/[eventId]/orders/new?service=<sku_code>` reusing the 0034 apply-then-pay flow. (6) Three SKU drifts logged for catch-up by the next Cowork pass: iteration `0011_panood.md` lists Same-Day Edit at **₱24,999** but `service_catalog` (V1 lock 2026-05-16) has it at **₱9,999** — page renders the catalog number (single source of truth) and the spec line is stale; iteration spec also lists `custom_monogram_pack` + `broadcast_style_pack` + `pro_camera_bridge_addon` SKUs that are absent from the current `service_catalog` seed (cut from V1 per the 2026-05-16 BYO-YouTube pivot but the spec body still mentions them in section bodies); iteration spec still has a `token_display: 60000` line in the wallet-integration block which is stale per the 2026-05-11 token-wallet retirement (no UI consequence — the page surfaces PHP only). | Three drivers. **First, the existing detail surface jumps straight to broadcaster setup,** which assumes the couple already owns Panood — there is no discovery layer for a couple who's never broadcast before. The App Store pattern is the well-known design language for "here's a thing you might buy" detail pages and lets us bring the comparison, the social proof, the privacy disclosures, and the plan picker onto a single coherent screen. **Second, the same template solves the vendor service detail problem cleanly** — when a couple opens an individual service from a vendor's profile, they need the same shape of info (preview screenshots, sample work, plans, reviews, privacy). | 2026-05-17 | **Event date-change flow with booked vendors — multi-party state machine locked.** Customer-facing date edits route through a confirmation gate that triggers only when the event has **≥1 confirmed vendor** (cart/draft don't count toward the threshold; mediation-state vendors do). The gate is a single modal with the affected-vendor list + a required reason field (min 30 chars). On submit: schedule check runs against each vendor's calendar; couple sees one of two messages — *"Your schedule change is available for all vendors. Waiting for their confirmation."* OR *"Your schedule change is available for X vendors but conflicts for Y vendors. We cannot apply this change until all vendors accept."* Pending state freezes everything (original date holds on both sides, no further date attempts by couple, payments paused, vendor slots locked from re-allocation). Vendor decline does NOT auto-fail the request — it routes the booking into the existing customer↔vendor chat thread (per the customer-initiates-chat rule), which gains a **structured action card** with Propose alternate / Accept this date / Cancel booking / Escalate to support buttons. Free-text agreements in chat are not load-bearing — only the action cards trigger state transitions, otherwise bookings sit frozen indefinitely. Timeouts both ways: vendor ghost past **48 hr** → auto-escalate to admin mediation tier (0023 Disputes Handler joins the thread, same pattern as the force-majeure flow in 0019 + the refund/dispute menu in iteration 0021 § 2.2); couple ghost past **72 hr** of active chat negotiation → request auto-cancels and event reverts to original date. Mediation outcomes (mediator selects from a fixed enum, no free-text resolutions): vendor reconsiders, couple stays on original date, vendor swap, full refund + cancellation of that vendor only, reschedule-fee compromise. Race condition: if a vendor backs out *during* an active date-change negotiation and that drops the confirmed-vendor count to zero, the in-flight negotiation auto-resolves and the couple is free to apply the change immediately. When the count transitions ≥1 → 0 for any reason (last vendor backs out, mediation cancels everyone, all vendors released), a passive "All vendors have been released — you can now change your event date freely" banner surfaces on the dashboard Home; dismisses on first date-edit attempt or after 14 days. Reschedule fees: vendors enter their per-window policy at onboarding (0006); V1 leaves fee enforcement as a manual mediator action (auto-debit lands in 0034 Phase 2). Hard cap of **2 date changes** per event lifecycle; third attempt is gated behind admin override via 0029 help center. Locked into iteration 0021 § 10 (new section). | Wedding-date changes are emotionally and contractually high-stakes — Filipino weddings involve venue deposits, vendor schedules booked 8–12 months out, and family travel logistics. A naive "edit and save" date field would either lock couples out of legitimate changes (force majeure, family emergency, venue issue) or break vendor trust by moving the date without their input. Routing both sides through structured negotiation surfaces (modal → schedule check → vendor confirm → chat with action cards → admin mediation) preserves vendor agency without leaving couples stranded, captures a reason for every change (audit trail + vendor empathy + admin dispute pattern detection), and reuses existing chat + force-majeure mediation infrastructure rather than building a parallel surface. Affects iterations: 0021 (couple dashboard — canonical spec, new § 10), 0006 (vendor side — receives the request action card + reschedule policy capture), 0019 (chat infrastructure — must support structured/interactive action cards as a first-class message type), 0023 (admin console — mediation tier + dispute ticket reuse), 0034 (payment freeze during pending state · auto-debit of reschedule fees deferred to Phase 2). |

| 2026-05-17 | **Event guest-count change flow — monotonic ratchet with vendor confirmation on increases, decreases blocked outright.** Guest count is a numeric attribute, not a swap, so the state machine diverges from § 10 / § 11 in two material ways: **(1)** changes are **direction-restricted** — couples can increase the planning guest count but cannot decrease it once any guest-count-dependent vendor has confirmed at that count. The minus stepper on the guest-count field is disabled at the UI layer with hint *"Cannot decrease below confirmed floor — vendors have already committed to N guests"* (mirrors the disabled-CTA pattern from § 2.2d.i self-review block). **(2)** the change touches only **guest-count-dependent vendors** — a per-vendor flag (`is_guest_count_dependent`) captured at onboarding (0006) marks which vendors plan against the count: defaults TRUE for catering, florals, mobile bar, lights & sound, name cards, favors, printable invites; defaults FALSE for photography, videography, HMUA, planner, broadcast. Only dependent vendors receive the confirmation card and only their capacity / pricing recalculates. **Ratchet enforcement:** floor = MAX(all confirmed counts ever in this event's history). New vendors booked later inherit the current floor as their starting commitment. Vendor back-out dissolves THAT vendor's commitment but the floor for remaining dependent vendors stays — couples cannot reduce because other vendors are still planning at the higher count. **Confirmation gate (only on increase):** modal surfaces per-vendor cost impact (e.g., "+20 plates × ₱1,200 = +₱24,000 for Casa Manila Catering") and total delta before vendor cards fire. **Per-vendor check is a capacity check** — does this vendor have the headcount capacity at the current proximity to event? Customer-facing messaging: *"Your guest count change is available for all vendors. Waiting for their confirmation."* OR *"Your guest count change is available for X vendors but exceeds capacity for Y vendors. We cannot apply this change until all vendors accept."* Same chat negotiation / mediation tier / 48 hr · 72 hr timeouts / race condition handling as § 10. **Decrease override:** couples experiencing genuine catastrophic cancellation (force majeure, mass family withdrawal) can request a floor reduction via 0029 help center → admin mediator works with each affected vendor case-by-case to negotiate downward; default behavior remains decrease-blocked. Locked into iteration 0021 § 12 (new section). | Caterers, florists, printers, and mobile-bar operators commit inventory + crew based on the guest count: ingredients pre-ordered, centerpieces fabricated, name cards printed, crew rostered. A late decrease causes irrecoverable financial loss for the vendor (perishable inventory + non-refundable supplier deposits) without a corresponding refund for the couple. The ratchet protects vendor margin while preserving couple flexibility on the only direction that's still possible (upward — vendors can scale up by sourcing more inventory). Direction-restriction is enforced at the UI rather than negotiated through the state machine because it's not a "vendor preference" issue — it's a physical commitment-of-inventory issue that mediation cannot reverse. The admin-override path covers genuine catastrophes where the couple has no alternative. Affects iterations: 0021 (canonical spec, new § 12), 0006 (vendor side — `is_guest_count_dependent` flag + per-head rate · capacity ceiling at proximity-to-event · capacity confirmation card), 0019 (chat infrastructure — same structured-card dependency as § 10), 0023 (admin mediation tier — decrease-override workflow), 0034 (per-head delta charges → existing milestone-payment flow). |
| 2026-05-17 | **Per-vendor change-acceptance cutoffs — vendors set three cutoff windows (date / venue / guest count) at onboarding; if any confirmed vendor is past their cutoff for the change type, the standard change flow is blocked outright and routes to admin override.** Each vendor record carries three fields captured at onboarding (0006): `date_change_cutoff_days_before_event`, `venue_change_cutoff_days_before_event`, `guest_count_change_cutoff_days_before_event` (NULL when vendor isn't dependent on the attribute). **V1 ships with conservative category-based defaults pre-filled at vendor account creation** — vendors edit in 0022 Settings: catering 30/21/14 days · florals 21/14/10 · mobile bar 21/14/7 · lights & sound 14/21/7 · photography 7/3/NULL · videography 7/3/NULL · HMUA 7/3/NULL · planner 7/3/7 · live stream / broadcast 3/3/NULL · name cards/favors/print 21/14/10. **Pre-flight gate on every change attempt** (date / venue / guest count): before the § 10.1 / § 11.1 / § 12.3 confirmation modal fires, the system checks each confirmed vendor's cutoff for the change type vs current proximity to event date. If any vendor is past their cutoff, the standard flow is blocked with a dedicated modal listing the blocking vendors + their cutoff dates + a "Request admin override" CTA — no reason field, no vendor cards. Admin override is the only forward path. **In-flight protection:** changes initiated BEFORE the cutoff date and currently pending continue to run to completion even if the cutoff falls during the negotiation window; cutoffs apply to NEW attempts, not in-progress ones (otherwise mid-window cutoff transitions would auto-fail valid changes). **Retroactivity rule:** vendor edits to their cutoffs in 0022 do NOT apply retroactively to already-confirmed bookings. Cutoffs in effect at booking-confirmation time are snapshotted to `vendor_event_window.effective_date_cutoff` / `effective_venue_cutoff` / `effective_guest_count_cutoff` and become binding for that event. Prevents vendors from quietly shortening their acceptance window mid-engagement to block the couple. **Admin override (only forward path past cutoff):** couple files via 0029 help center → admin mediator reaches out to each past-cutoff vendor individually → if vendors agree, mediator applies the change via 0023 admin console; if vendors decline, the couple's only remaining option is to cancel that vendor's booking and find a replacement. Override actions log to `dispute_resolutions` with `cause = 'past_cutoff_override'`. **Out of scope:** cutoffs apply only to vendor bookings — Setnayan platform SKUs (Papic, Panood, Patiktok, LED, AI Highlights, etc.) have their own pre-event activation / rendering / fulfillment windows handled separately by the per-SKU flows. Locked into iteration 0021 § 13 (new section) with cross-references added to § 10, § 11, § 12. | Vendor margin protection: as the event approaches, vendors progressively commit inventory and crew — catering buys ingredients, florists buy flowers, lights & sound rosters crew, printers run name cards. Late-stage changes can be unrecoverable financial losses. The cutoff lets vendors declare upfront what proximity is too late for what kind of change, removing the negotiation tax (and the awkward "we have to say no" interaction) for changes that are physically impossible to accommodate at that proximity. **Defaults eliminate vendor configuration burden** for the common case — most catering vendors won't think to set a cutoff manually, but the V1 seed values match industry norms (caterers commonly lock headcount 14 days out; photographers can adapt to date changes within a week). **The retroactivity rule closes an adversarial edge case** — without it, a vendor unhappy with a potential reschedule could shorten their cutoff to 90 days the moment they sensed friction, instantly blocking the couple. Snapshotting cutoffs at booking confirmation means the terms that existed when the couple chose this vendor are the binding ones. **Admin override preserves couple agency** for genuine emergencies (typhoon, venue collapse, family crisis) while keeping the default flow tight and protecting vendors from frivolous late-stage requests. Affects iterations: 0021 (canonical spec, new § 13 + cross-refs in § 10/§ 11/§ 12), 0006 (vendor onboarding — three new cutoff fields with category-based defaults), 0022 (vendor dashboard — Change Acceptance Policy settings panel · NOT retroactive to confirmed bookings), 0023 (admin override workflow + `dispute_resolutions.cause = 'past_cutoff_override'`), 0029 (help center — past-cutoff override request form). |

The mismatch between DB enum semantics + UI semantics is documented inline in `apps/web/lib/contracts.ts` so future engineers reading the code understand why the enum value name is stale. **(3) New UI copy makes the externality of signing explicit + load-bearing.** Vendor detail page reads *"Setnayan hosts this PDF for the couple to reference — we do not facilitate signing. Handle signatures externally (email, in-person, your own e-sig tool) and keep the signed copy with your records."* Couple detail page mirrors it with vendor-attribution: *"This contract was uploaded by {vendor} for your reference. Setnayan hosts the PDF so both sides have a copy on hand — signing happens between you and the vendor outside the app (email, in-person, or your own e-sig tool). Keep a signed copy with your records."* Both blocks treat the externality of signing as the primary message, not a fine-print disclaimer — that's the brand-voice + liability posture this row locks in. List pages on both sides + the publish CTA label ("Make visible to couple") reinforce the same framing. **(4) Why the owner made this call** (drivers behind the further shrink, beyond the verbatim quote above). **First, signing isn't Setnayan's core competency** — wedding-planning artifacts (timeline, vendor pack, Concierge wizard, Save-the-Date, Panood, Patiktok) are the value Setnayan ships; e-signature is a commodity feature already solved by DocuSign · HelloSign · Adobe Sign · Signaturit · plus free workarounds (emailing a signed scan, in-person signing at vendor meetings) that the wedding industry already uses comfortably. Building it in-house gates Setnayan against best-in-class e-sig tooling for no upside, and bundling it as a Setnayan feature signals to couples + vendors that the app is the contract authority — which it isn't. **Second, liability scope shrinks substantially.** A dual-sig flow where Setnayan captures + stores signature PNGs + IP + UA + signed_at + serves them via signed URLs makes Setnayan an arguable party to the contract's execution (or at minimum a custodian of e-signature evidence) under Philippine Electronic Commerce Act (RA 8792) + Rules on Electronic Evidence — even with disclaimers, a couple or vendor in dispute could subpoena Setnayan as evidence custodian, force preservation orders, and surface the platform as a third-party in litigation. Pure document hosting (PDF storage with view/download access) keeps Setnayan in the same posture as Dropbox or Google Drive — a passive document host with no signature authority. **Third, simpler UX for both sides.** Vendors already upload signed PDFs to clients via email constantly — adding a "sign in Setnayan" step is friction, not value. Couples likewise prefer to read + sign on their own time + with their own tooling (e.g., printing for traditional ink signature with family witnesses present, as is common in Filipino wedding contracts). The Setnayan flow shrinks to upload → publish → both sides can see/download → done, which fits naturally alongside the chat thread where the contract was negotiated. **Fourth, couples and vendors handle signing flows wherever they prefer** — the spec does not need to pick a signing UX for the entire ecosystem; the wedding industry's existing patterns (email signed PDFs, in-person at venue site visits, separate e-sig tool for traveling couples) cover the spectrum without Setnayan opining. | 2026-05-19 | **0018 business-model pivot — marketplace-commission (10-15%) → Setnayan-sourced resale (50% markup on wholesale ≈ 33% of retail). Iteration brand renamed "Supplies Marketplace" → "Setnayan Supplies". Spec body rewritten; SPEC_COMPLETION_BRIEF replaced with proper ENGINEERING_BRIEF in the 0018 worktree.** Owner directive: "the goal is to have our internal service (usually the nearest vendors that can print near the customer's area) that is under us · we will have direct contact with them for purchases · we will agree on a price · the agreed price will depend on the vendor · so different areas may have different prices · whatever their price is for us, we will charge an additional 50% of their service · ALL SKUs are Setnayan-sourced resale (50% markup uniformly)." **What changed:** (1) Business model — Setnayan is now the CURATED RESELLER, not a marketplace operator. Setnayan negotiates wholesale prices with supplier vendors per service area, marks up 50% on wholesale, sells to couples at retail = wholesale × 1.5. (2) Customer relationship — couples buy from Setnayan, NOT from supplier vendors; supplier vendor identity may not even be surfaced to couples (or only post-order for support cases). Setnayan owns all customer support, returns, disputes, refunds. (3) Vendor payout — wholesale paid out by Setnayan after order completes (T+7 default); NOT retail-minus-commission. (4) BIR treatment — Setnayan issues OR for full retail (not commission); supplier vendor invoices Setnayan at wholesale separately; Form 2307 obligations shift to "Setnayan issues 2307 to supplier vendor as supplier, not as marketplace seller". (5) Revenue model — 50% markup on wholesale ≈ 33% of retail ≈ 25-30% net margin after support cost. Indicative scale: 1,000 orders/month × ₱1,500 avg retail × 33% margin ≈ **₱495K/month gross margin** (substantially higher than original commission model's ~₱180K/month at same volume). (6) Owner-side ops requirement — Setnayan must build supplier-vendor relationships PER AREA PER SKU category before launch. Minimum gating: 1-3 supplier vendors per category per service area for V1 Metro Manila. Without signed wholesale agreements + entered wholesale prices, the surface stays behind a "Coming to your area soon — join waitlist" empty state. (7) Schema impact — NEW tables: `supplier_vendor_skus` · `supplier_vendor_sku_pricing` (with `service_area_code` + `wholesale_centavos` + `volume_tiers` + `effective_from`/`effective_to`) · `supplies_orders` (with `total_retail_centavos` + `total_wholesale_centavos` + `total_markup_centavos`) · `supplies_order_line_items` (with `wholesale_centavos_at_order` + `retail_centavos_at_order` snapshot for price-change protection). (11) Files updated this row — `0018_supplies_marketplace/0018_supplies_marketplace.md` (full rewrite — model pivot framing at top + new category/wholesale table + supplier vendor onboarding flow + schema additions + cross-iteration impacts + anti-abuse + pre-launch gate checklist) · `0018-supplies-marketplace` worktree `SPEC_COMPLETION_BRIEF.md` DELETED + `ENGINEERING_BRIEF.md` CREATED (commit replaces the placeholder brief from earlier today; ~235 lines covering 8 PR plan + schema migrations + cross-iteration impacts + don'ts) · `App_Build_Status.md` row update pending. `Setnayan_Supplier_Vendor_Agreement.md` template TO BE DRAFTED in `01_Contracts/` — flagged as owner-side blocker. **Engineering can proceed in parallel with owner-side vendor agreement work** — PRs 1-8 ship; surface stays gated behind "Coming to your area soon" empty state until first supplier vendor signs + wholesale prices entered in admin surface. **Higher-yield pivot is net-positive vs original commission model:** roughly 2.7× the gross margin at the same order volume, but requires owner-side ops investment to build supplier-vendor relationships per area. **Sequencing note:** spec rewrite + engineering brief replacement · no app code · no schema migrations · no SKU changes · 0018 worktree branch `claude/0018-supplies-marketplace` now has proper `ENGINEERING_BRIEF.md` committed (replaces earlier `SPEC_COMPLETION_BRIEF.md`) · `.docx` mirror regeneration deferred per established convention. | Owner directive 2026-05-19 — confirmed via AskUserQuestion ("ALL SKUs are Setnayan-sourced resale (50% markup uniformly)"). **First, this pivot dramatically improves Setnayan's economics on the physical-side surface.** Marketplace commission of 10-15% leaves most of the retail price with the vendor — vendor sets retail at, say, ₱1,500 and Setnayan earns ₱150-225. Resale at wholesale × 1.5 with wholesale ₱1,000 means Setnayan earns ₱500 (after passing ₱1,000 wholesale to vendor), or ~3× the commission take. At pilot scale this is the difference between Supplies being a small ancillary revenue line vs a meaningful margin contributor. **Second, the resale model gives Setnayan complete control over couple experience.** In the marketplace model, vendors were the customer-facing party — vendor handles support, fulfillment communication, returns. That creates inconsistent CX (some vendors fast/professional, others slow/disorganized) and constantly puts Setnayan brand at risk because couples blame Setnayan for vendor failures. In the resale model, Setnayan owns the whole journey — couples experience uniform Setnayan-branded service regardless of which supplier fulfilled. Service quality becomes a Setnayan operations problem (manageable) instead of a vendor-quality problem (uncontrollable). **Third, area-based wholesale pricing is the right model for PH geography.** Print + rental costs vary significantly by area (Manila CBD vs Cebu vs Davao); a one-price-fits-all retail would either over-charge customers in low-cost areas OR under-deliver margin in high-cost areas. Per-area wholesale + uniform 50% markup means retail naturally adjusts to local costs while Setnayan's margin stays constant. **Fourth, the model is operationally heavier but the math justifies it.** Setnayan now carries supplier-vendor relationship management as an ongoing ops cost — finding suppliers, negotiating wholesale, signing agreements, monitoring SLA, managing backups. That's ~5-15% of leadership/ops time once the supplier base reaches ~20-30 vendors. The 2.7× margin uplift more than pays for that ops cost — at 1,000 orders/month, the extra ~₱315K/month over commission model would fund ops capacity directly. **Fifth, the model creates a defensibility moat.** Marketplace platforms are commoditized — vendors can multi-home easily. A curated-reseller model with negotiated wholesale agreements creates real switching costs for vendors (they can't just leave for a competitor that offers higher retail rates because their wholesale agreement with Setnayan locks in volume + payment terms). Vendors also get value from Setnayan (consistent demand + payment certainty + brand association). | 2026-05-22 | **Fix: Reception planning-group Search showed Ceremony churches above target section (Task #47 · PR [#310](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/310) merged 2026-05-22).** Fourth 2026-05-22 row · live-bug report from owner during V1 marketplace testing: *"i am searching for reception venue and the churches still showed. they are not qualified because they are design for ceremonies"*. **Root cause** (none of the 4 initial candidates exactly — actual cause was page-level rendering scope): `/vendors` rendered the full 12-folder catalog on every visit regardless of how the user arrived. `WEDDING_FOLDER_ORDER` lists Ceremony first (with `<PairedVenuePanel>` page-level + `<CeremonyVenuesSection>` inside the Ceremony folder showing church/mosque/INC-chapel/civil-registrar cards from `venue_directory`), then Reception. When dashboard event-home Reception planning-group [Search] button routed to `/vendors#reception`, the browser scroll-anchored to the Reception `<section id="reception">` heading — but the entire Ceremony folder + the page-level PairedVenuePanel sat directly above. | 2026-05-22 | **Fix: Planning-card picks now flag incompatibility when host's wedding type or venue setting drifts away — inline amber chip + Remove form-button on each affected pick (Task #53 · PR [#315](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/315) merged 2026-05-22).** Tenth 2026-05-22 row · PR B of the Tasks #51-#55 bundle (5-dimension card filtering overhaul). PR A (PR #314, merged same session) closed Dimensions 1+2+4; this PR closes **Dimension 3** — picks whose `compatible_ceremony_types[]` / `compatible_venue_settings[]` arrays don't cover the host's current `events.ceremony_type` / `events.venue_setting` now surface an inline amber chip below the pick row with a polite-voice explanation + a Remove form-button. Owner directive verbatim: *"surface mismatches as a chip on the picked-item row with a Remove action. Don't auto-delete — the host gets agency."* **Why this matters structurally:** PR #306 (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-22 row 5) unlocked editing `ceremony_type` while 0 vendors are confirmed, which means a host can flip catholic → civil OR banquet_hall → garden AFTER they've saved a Catholic-church pick or a banquet-hall-only band. Without this flag, those picks would silently stay in the plan, leak into the Compare view + the day-of timeline, and ambush the host at lock-in. **Three issue kinds, ranked by severity:** (1) `religion` — marketplace-linked vendor's `vendor_profiles.compatible_ceremony_types[]` doesn't include host's current `ceremony_type` → chip reads *"Your wedding is now Civil — this vendor doesn't match."* (2) `venue_setting` — marketplace-linked vendor's `vendor_profiles.compatible_venue_settings[]` doesn't include host's current `venue_setting` → chip reads *"Your reception is now a garden — this vendor doesn't cover that setting."* (3) `directory` — picks linked via `event_vendors.source_venue_directory_id` (not `marketplace_vendor_id`) where `venue_directory.compatible_ceremony_types[]` mismatches → chip reads *"Your wedding is now Civil — this venue doesn't host that ceremony."* **Precedence: religion > venue_setting > directory.** A marketplace vendor failing both religion AND venue_setting surfaces the religion mismatch (more semantically severe). Venue-only mismatches surface only when religion would pass. **Null array convention** (open-to-all safety valve): an empty `compatible_*` array OR NULL column treats the vendor as compatible — same OR-clause shape as PR #305's `/vendors` religion-default-on filter (`compat IS NULL OR compat @> ARRAY[host_value]`). Protects legacy / pre-iteration-0043 vendor rows from false-positive flags. **Off-platform / custom rows** (no `marketplace_vendor_id` AND no `source_venue_directory_id`) → no compat data exists → chip never renders. **Data fetch strategy:** extended the `event_vendors` SELECT in `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/page.tsx` to include `marketplace_vendor_id` + `source_venue_directory_id` (no schema change — columns already exist via migrations `20260519200000_vendor_invites_foundation.sql` + `20260530000000_event_vendors_venue_directory_link.sql`). Two follow-up batch queries against `vendor_profiles` + `venue_directory` resolve the compat arrays via `.in('vendor_profile_id', marketplaceIds)` + `.in('venue_directory_id', directoryIds)`. At most 2 extra round trips per page render even for events with 50+ picks — mirrors the fetch pattern in `apps/web/lib/venue-recommendations.ts` (PR #309 lineage). Both helper queries use the existing `adminClient` since `vendor_profiles` + `venue_directory` are public-read tables. **Brand voice — amber not red.** This is informational, not an error. The vendor was a valid pick when the host saved them; the *event* changed underneath them, so the chip reads as a heads-up not a scolding. AlertTriangle icon + amber-50/60 background + amber-300/50 border + Remove button styled as a calm cream-filled border-amber-400/60 micro-button. Per [[feedback_setnayan_no_dev_text_post_launch]] — no jargon, no inline parens, just one polite sentence + a single-word action. **Remove flow:** reuses the existing `deleteVendor` server action in `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/vendors/actions.ts` (host clicks Remove → form submits hidden `event_id` + `vendor_id` → server action runs under host's RLS session → row hard-deleted from `event_vendors` → revalidates both `/dashboard/[eventId]` AND `/dashboard/[eventId]/vendors` so chip vanishes without a hard refresh). Hard-delete is intentional here — the host has explicitly opted to remove an incompatible pick that no longer matches their event. No new server action, no new endpoints — orphan-free by construction. **Schema additions in `apps/web/lib/wedding-plan-groups.ts`:** new `PlanCardCompatibilityIssue` discriminated union type · new `EventVendorRowInput` shape that captures the joined compat arrays · new `computeCompatibilityIssue(row, eventCeremonyType, eventVenueSetting)` algorithm (religion check first via marketplace_compatible_ceremony_types, then venue_setting check via marketplace_compatible_venue_settings, then directory fallback via directory_compatible_ceremony_types, otherwise null) · `bucketVendorsByGroup()` signature widened with two optional args (`eventCeremonyType`, `eventVenueSetting`) so the compat check is computed inline during bucketing (zero extra iteration overhead). `CEREMONY_TYPE_READABLE_LABEL` + `VENUE_SETTING_READABLE_LABEL` copy tables provide human-readable labels matching the existing `ceremony-type-chip.tsx` + `/vendors/page.tsx VENUE_SETTING_LABEL` wording so terminology stays consistent across the dashboard. **Entry points (orphan-prevention per [[feedback_setnayan_orphan_prevention]]):** `/dashboard/[eventId]` event home (planning-cards section). The `CompatibilityChip` is a sub-element of an existing card pick row; it renders only when `pick.compatibility_issue` is non-null. Remove form wires to the existing `deleteVendor` server action — no new routes, no new endpoints, no new orphan risk. **Test plan:** `pnpm -F web typecheck` clean · `pnpm -F web lint` no new warnings (same pre-existing in `color-range-manipulator.tsx`) · visual smoke pending post-deploy preview but covers: (a) Catholic event with Catholic church pick → no chip (compatible); (b) flip ceremony_type → Civil via CeremonyTypeChip modal → Catholic church pick now shows amber chip + Remove button; (c) Garden `venue_setting` event with indoor-only-tagged band → chip with venue mismatch + Remove; (d) click Remove → row + chip vanish, no full page refresh, counter math adjusts; (e) off-platform vendor with both FKs null → no chip regardless of event drift. **Affected files** (4 files net +429/-51): `apps/web/lib/wedding-plan-groups.ts` (PlanCardCompatibilityIssue type + EventVendorRowInput shape + computeCompatibilityIssue algorithm + readable-label tables + bucketVendorsByGroup widened signature) · `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/page.tsx` (extend events SELECT to include `venue_setting` · extend event_vendors SELECT to include `marketplace_vendor_id` + `source_venue_directory_id` · two batch-fetch queries for compat data · enrich event_vendors rows before PlanningGroups consumes them · pass `venueSetting` + `ceremonyType` props) · `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/_components/planning-groups.tsx` (thread `venueSetting` prop · pass to bucketVendorsByGroup · new CompatibilityChip sub-component with AlertTriangle icon + amber palette + form action=deleteVendor) · `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/vendors/actions.ts` (deleteVendor now also revalidates `/dashboard/[eventId]` event-home path so chip vanishes without hard refresh). **Auto-merge** per [[feedback_setnayan_pr_auto_merge]] — `gh pr merge 315 --auto --merge` armed immediately after creation. **Cross-references:** CLAUDE.md 2026-05-22 row 9 above (PR #314 PR A — Dimensions 1+2+4 ship same session) · CLAUDE.md 2026-05-22 row 5 (PR #305 religion-default-on filter on /vendors — same compatibility shape; Owner directive verbatim: *"desktop mode will have 2 columns (to maximize screen size) while mobile mode will only have 1 column."* **(1) Change.** Grid class on the tier-loop `<ul>` rewrote from `grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-4` → `grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2`. Mobile (<640px) keeps grid-cols-1 unchanged; sm: (≥640px) + every wider breakpoint locks at grid-cols-2; the lg: (1024px) jump to 3 cols + xl: (1280px) jump to 4 cols are removed. **(2) Why.** With 12 planning cards grouped across 4 tiers (per [[CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20 "Home is the guide" row]] · latest-by floors + front-load compression + completed-tasks-sink), each card carries a title + religion-adaptive hint copy (from PR #314 · 2026-05-22 row 9) + status pill + tone-coded badge + pick list with possible incompatibility chip (from PR #315 · 2026-05-22 row 10). At lg/xl breakpoints each card was 240-340px wide which forced the religion-adaptive Muslim hint copy + Catholic pre-Cana paperwork hint + similar long-copy lines to wrap awkwardly into 3+ lines. At sm: 2-col the cards are 320-630px wide depending on viewport — enough horizontal room for the longest religion-adaptive copy + the pick list previews + the inline incompatibility chip. Trade-off accepted: laptops + wide monitors now show 2-col stack instead of 4-col grid, which means the page is taller on a 1440px viewport — but per the owner directive *"maximize screen size"* refers to per-card horizontal real-estate, not vertical density. Vertical scroll is OK; cramped cards are not. **(3) Entry points (orphan-prevention per [[feedback_setnayan_orphan_prevention]]):** `/dashboard/[eventId]` event home — every host's first surface after login per [[project_setnayan_login_landing]]. Owner directive across this session: *"i am at the mood board. where is it"* → screenshot showing the Wedding Attire Guide section MISSING despite source code on main (PR #446/#447 rendering bug) → *"we want it to be better looking. feels like a cheap look like a 2 yr old drew it"* (figure polish ask) → *"also the styles are not changing"* (style picker chips were inert placeholders) → owner shares Pinterest "WEDDING GUEST DRESSES" collage of 10 Western-model pastel dresses + *"i want something like this but we can alter the color of the dress and have a flipina face and same to the men"* (real photo + Filipino face + recolorable + men too). **(1) PR #449 IIFE-suppressed render fix.** Diagnosis: async server component (`<VisualPreviewSection>`) + client component (`<WeddingAttireGuide>`) siblings inside an IIFE-returned fragment silently fail to mount through the RSC boundary in React 19 + Next.js 15. Fix: hoist `flatPalette` out of the IIFE to the data-prep block + render both components as flat top-level JSX siblings. The IIFE was the fragile pattern; flat top-level JSX is the reliable shape. Architecture insight captured for future sessions. **(2) PR #451 figure polish (closed/superseded by #453).** Rebuilt Silhouette function with 6-layer rendering: (1) ground shadow ellipse beneath feet · (2) hair path BEHIND head (long flowing for dress; short cropped for suit/barong) · (3) skin-tone head circle (r=6 vs prior r=5 for better proportions) · (4) body path with smooth bezier curves per attire type (fitted bodice + A-line skirt on dress, jacket + trousers + hinted leg split on suit, loose vertical with subtle bell hem on barong) · (5) per-attire detail overlays (neckline V on dress, lapel V + tie on suit, embroidery dashed line on barong) · (6) two small shoe ovals at the foot. Canvas got radial gradient + decorative pointed-arch SVG at bottom. ViewBox 0 0 28 92 for elegant tall proportions (vs prior 24 60 which produced squat cartoonish figures). PR #451 was closed in favor of PR #453 which subsumed all of #451's polish PLUS the new style-themes work. **(3) PR #453 StyleTheme system.** Style picker chips were inert toggles; this PR wires each chip to a concrete `StyleTheme` record that drives visible aesthetic changes. New `StyleTheme` type with 7 properties (hairTint · shoeTint · background · innerShadow · archStroke · archStrokeWidth · archStyle · bodyStrokeOpacity) and 5 themes mapped to the 5 STYLE_OPTIONS chips (`elegant·simple·classic` / `bridgerton·regal` / `editorial cream` / `tropical heritage` / `modern minimalist`). New `CanvasArches` component renders one of 5 venue archetypes based on `theme.archStyle` ('pointed' = 3 gothic chapel arches · 'romanesque' = 3 rounded full arches · 'minimal' = 6 thin tick marks · 'natural' = 2 palm fronds + sun arc · 'absent' = early-return null). Canvas got `transition-all duration-500` for smooth crossfade between styles. Body path stroke binds to `theme.bodyStrokeOpacity` instead of hardcoded value. Each chip click now visibly shifts: canvas background, inner shadow, hair tint, shoe tint, body stroke opacity, venue arch decoration. Architecture: V1.x AI engine will use the active style as part of the Higgsfield prompt (e.g., "bridgerton-regal romantic period setting with rich jewel tones"); today's map gives couples visible feedback that the picker is real + lets them feel the aesthetic shift the AI engine will eventually render fully. **(4) PR #455 stacked-into-#453 photo swap.** Owner picked via AskUserQuestion: **single figure per role** (current layout, not new Pinterest multi-option grid) + **curated Pexels stock photos** (V1 placeholder path per the locked 2026-05-21 Dress codes 3-phase strategy: internet placeholders → V1.x Higgsfield Filipino-specific → V1.x+ stylist real uploads). **What ships:** new `RoleAsset` type + `assetsByRole` optional prop on `WeddingAttireGuide`; new `PhotoFigure` renderer component — plain `<img>` with absolutely-positioned `mix-blend-mode: multiply` overlay div (background = tint · opacity 0.55) for visible recolor feedback when host picks a color (V1 honest path: multiplies photo pixels by picked color, light areas/dress fabric take the tint while darker areas/skin/hair keep their natural value); `RoleCluster` branches — when asset present, renders ONE PhotoFigure with `× N` count badge for `role.count > 1` (vs N copies of same photo = Warhol-print effect that looks bad); `mood-board/page.tsx` fetches `moodboard_library_assets` filtered by `asset_type='figure_attire'` joined to slot-1 `sampled_hex`, builds `assetsByRole` map keyed by `asset_subtype`, threads to component; new migration `20260611000000_iteration_0010_attire_guide_filipino_seed.sql` inserts 10 `figure_attire` rows (one per `RoleKey`: bride · groom · bridesmaids · groomsmen · female_ps · male_ps · mothers · fathers · guests · men_guests) using free-commercial Pexels CDN URLs + pre-tagged slot-1 `sampled_hex` per asset. **Migration pushed to prod** via `supabase db push --linked` per [[feedback_setnayan_push_migrations_myself]] — confirmed live on `setnayan-prod` (last applied: `20260611000000`). **Pexels availability honest note:** Filipino-specific stock model availability is genuinely limited on free stock sites. The 4 highest-impact roles (bride · groom · female_ps · male_ps) use Filipino-tagged photos (e.g., Pexels 22601419 "Filipino man in barong tagalog" · 37706671 "Filipina formal gown at floral table setting" · 12886228 "Asian bride with bouquet" · 24551674 "Asian groom traditional attire"). Bridesmaids · groomsmen · guests use pan-Asian or generic stock — supply skews Western. V1.x Higgsfield batch generation per the 2026-05-21 lock will swap the full library to Filipino-specific renders. **(5) Recolor approach reasoning.** Pure photo recoloring is hard without canvas image processing (V1.x Color Range Manipulator approach via HSL substitution keyed on per-asset sampled_hex). For V1 chose CSS mix-blend-multiply because (a) zero-dependency · zero-compute · works in every browser · (b) visible enough that picking a color obviously does something even if not pixel-perfect · (c) skin gets a slight color cast which is acceptable trade-off for V1 placeholder; the alternative (`filter: hue-rotate()`) only works for already-colored attire and breaks on white wedding gowns shifting to burgundy. V1.x Color Range Manipulator engine swaps to proper region-specific canvas substitution; today's CSS overlay is the V1-placeholder honest path. **(6) Scope check.** Lands inside the LOCKED Dress codes pillar of iteration 0010 per the 2026-05-21 row ("tagged figure photos with clothing recolored via role palettes"). | 2026-05-23 | **Fix: Invited-to chips on guest forms get role-based smart defaults via client island — inner-circle roles (couple · parents · immediate family · MOH/MoH/Best Man · bridesmaid · groomsman · principal sponsor · 12 roles) default to all 5 blocks · everyone else (secondary sponsors · bearers · flower girl · readers · soloist · plain guest · 12 roles) defaults to ceremony + reception + cocktails (PR [#433](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/433) merged 2026-05-23).** Fourth 2026-05-23 row · Path 2 from the multi-turn Invited-to walkthrough that closed with owner asking *"do we need to define this? if yes, please justify. should they all be invited to all?"* + my 3-path response. Path 2 ships smart defaults today without schema work; Path 1 (event-level toggles + role defaults · `events.schedule_includes_cocktails / _after_party / _rehearsal_dinner` booleans) deferred until owner picks the event-level scope. **Why the change matters:** prior behavior hardcoded `defaultChecked={block === 'ceremony' || block === 'reception'}` for every guest regardless of role — every VIP forced 3+ extra clicks (cocktails + after-party + rehearsal dinner). At typical Filipino wedding sizes (50-300 guests · ~10-20 inner-circle) that's 30-60 wasted clicks per event for the inner circle alone, plus another 1 click per non-inner-circle guest (cocktails). Per the Filipino-wedding-reality analysis: 95-100% of guests attend ceremony + reception + cocktails regardless of role; only the inner circle attends after-party + rehearsal-dinner by default. **Schema (zero changes):** no new columns · no new tables · no new SKU · `invited_${block}` checkbox names on the form stay identical so server actions consume them unchanged. **Code (4 files net +182/-37):** `apps/web/lib/guests.ts` — new `INNER_CIRCLE_ROLES` `ReadonlySet<GuestRole>` (12 roles: bride · groom · bride_parents · groom_parents · bride_immediate_family · groom_immediate_family · maid_of_honor · matron_of_honor · best_man · bridesmaid · groomsman · principal_sponsor) + new exported `defaultInvitedToForRole(role: GuestRole): InvitedToBlock[]` helper (returns 5-block array for inner-circle roles, 3-block array `['ceremony', 'reception', 'cocktails']` for everyone else). `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/guests/_components/invited-to-chips.tsx` — NEW client island. Listens to the role `<select id="role">` on the same page via `document.getElementById` + `addEventListener('change')`. On mount: populates from `initialBlocks` (edit form · existing guest's saved value) OR `defaultInvitedToForRole(initialRole)` (new form · no saved value yet). On role change after mount: snaps chips to the new role's defaults. Controlled checkboxes (React `checked` prop) so Tailwind `has-[:checked]:` selectors still flip the chip background on snap. `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/guests/new/page.tsx` — swaps hardcoded chip JSX for `<InvitedToChips roleSelectId="role" initialRole="guest"/>`. Drops now-unused `INVITED_TO_BLOCKS` + `INVITED_TO_LABELS` imports. Hint copy updated from *"Default: ceremony + reception. Toggle off any block the guest isn't invited to"* to *"Picks smart defaults from the Role above. Toggle any block the guest isn't invited to."* `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/guests/[guestId]/page.tsx` — same swap with `<InvitedToChips roleSelectId="role" initialRole={guest.role} initialBlocks={initialInvited}/>` where `initialInvited` filters `guest.invited_to_blocks` (schema column is `string[]`) to valid `InvitedToBlock` values via type guard. Removes `INVITED_TO_LABELS` import (kept `INVITED_TO_BLOCKS` for the filter). **Snap-on-role-change behavior:** when host changes Role dropdown AFTER mount, chips snap to the new role's defaults. Host's prior manual toggles on the OLD role get reset — intentional trade-off because role change implies "this person's attendance scope is different now" (e.g., changing a guest from `bridesmaid` to `coin_sponsor` should reset after-party + rehearsal-dinner off, not keep them on by accident). Host can re-toggle individual chips after the snap. **Snap-NOT-on-mount behavior for edit form:** when `initialBlocks` is provided (edit form with existing guest data), chips populate from the saved value on first render — no snap. The snap only fires on subsequent role changes via the change-event listener. This preserves existing data correctly while still delivering smart defaults on role changes. **Inner-circle rationale:** the 12 roles chosen are the ones who attend after-party + rehearsal dinner in Filipino wedding reality (couple themselves · parents who host the event · immediate family who fly in · primary wedding party who's there for the prep + after · principal sponsors who're peer-witnesses). Secondary sponsors (candle/veil/cord/coin) typically attend ceremony only — they're peer-honors not full-event family; bearers + flower girl are kids whose parents manage their attendance separately; officiant + readers + soloist have ceremony roles but typically aren't invited to post-event social blocks. Host can still toggle on/off per individual guest where needed. **Cross-references:** CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20 row § "VIP family roles" PR #424 (added the 4 VIP family roles that are part of the inner-circle set) · CLAUDE.md 2026-05-22 row § "Concierge dual-scope trial" (similar client-island pattern · `document.getElementById` + `useEffect` listener on form interactions) · existing `INVITED_TO_BLOCKS` constant in `lib/guests.ts` (5-block enum order: ceremony · reception · cocktails · after_party · rehearsal_dinner — unchanged). **Path 1 still pending owner decision** (event-level toggles via `events.schedule_includes_cocktails / _after_party / _rehearsal_dinner` booleans). Tone is advisory not prescriptive — couples can always proceed with any date; the Brain's job is to surface what's true about it, not override the couple's choice. **(4) Primary-layer resolution table.** Locks how the Brain picks which curated 2-3 reasons surface as the headline based on intake signals — Catholic ceremony + devout → Catholic / Liturgical primary · Chinese-Filipino household → Numerology primary (+ Catholic if applicable) · OFW-heavy guest list → Practical (homecoming alignment) · budget-conscious → Practical (Friday rates) · astrologically inclined → Western Astrology primary · default fallback → Practical (universally applicable). Mixed-faith / interfaith uses Practical primary + Catholic + Numerology layered as applicable. **(5) Strategic positioning.** No competitor in PH wedding-tech (The Knot · Zola · Joy · WedMeGood · Bridestory · Bride and Breakfast) ships layered cultural date-reasoning. WedMeGood gives generic Hindu calendar overlay only; the rest give a happy emoji. Structured cultural depth is one of Setnayan's structural moats per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-19 row 425 (V1.1 content engine) + 2026-05-18 row 6 (Concierge AI Brain architecture). (2) `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/_components/wizard-cards/ceremony-venue-card.tsx` passed `events.venue_setting` (the host's RECEPTION venue type) into `fetchWizardVendorRecommendations` as a HARD filter. The author's own comment ("Ceremony venues aren't typically filtered by venue_setting") said this filter shouldn't apply — but the prop was passed through anyway. Result: any host with a non-heritage reception (banquet_hall / garden / beach / destination / outdoor_tent) saw the empty state. **Architectural error:** a ceremony venue's compatibility is about ceremony_type + faith, not the couple's reception style. Pivoted to `SET compatible_venue_settings = ARRAY[<7 reception settings>]` which achieves equivalent runtime behaviour without touching the schema. **Migration applied:** scoped via `WHERE user_id IS NULL AND services && ARRAY['religious_venue' OR 'officiant']` so any future real church account that claims its venue and intentionally sets compat tags is preserved. Idempotency keys on the `@>` superset check. **Belt-and-suspenders on Card 04 Officiant:** today every officiant in prod is tagged with all venue_settings (universal) so the code-side defensive pass changes nothing in current behaviour — but if a future seed narrows the tags the way the religious_venue seed did, Card 04 won't inherit the trap. **Post-fix verification:** Catholic + banquet_hall now returns **19** religious venues (was 0). All 7 reception venue_setting permutations × all 7 ceremony_types now surface the correct curated set. **Engineering investigation method (worth preserving for future debugging):** (a) confirmed Card 03 reads `vendor_market_stats` view filtering by `canonical_service='religious_venue'` (not `venue_directory` directly — that table is a separate spec for the deferred V1.2 venue marketplace); (b) confirmed 28 religious_venue rows in prod; (c) ran the exact server-side query the page fires for catholic + banquet_hall → 0 rows; (d) ran same query for catholic + heritage → 18 rows; (e) traced source to the seed migration's narrow tagging. **Engineering time:** ~15 min investigation + ~20 min coding/migration + ~5 min CI/auto-merge + ~5 min migration push + verify. Your Plan / Wizard surfaces render these as "✓ Included with {Vendor Name}'s {Package Name}" — visually distinct chip styling (cream-toned, no Remove button, click-to-view-parent-vendor instead of edit). Updated per-card hard-floor table at CLAUDE.md 2026-05-24 eighth row "Today's Focus SKU lock" stays canonical · 7 new rows append to its 38-entry table making it 45 entries · iteration `0016_step_by_step_plan_builder.md` table queued for matching update on next Cowork sync pass. **(2) Lock/delete/overlap architecture — 5 behavioral rules.** Owner directive verbatim: *"when we lock a vendor and open that vendor, it has details to show. for as long as there is no downpayment given, this vender can still be deleted. vendor can also delete the customer if they need to open the schedule. for vendors, if there is no locked schedule yet via downpayment. they can still accept inquiries for that schedule. and it will be their call if they will accept the request for overlap on schedule? or what do you suggest?"* Architecture maps onto the existing `VendorStatus` enum at `apps/web/lib/vendors.ts:35-41`: **`contracted` = SOFT HOLD (locked, no money yet) · `deposit_paid` = HARD LOCK (downpayment reconciled by admin)**. These two statuses already exist in production schema · what's new is the behavioral semantics layered on top. **Rule 1 · Host-side cancel pre-downpayment.** Vendor detail page on host side at `/dashboard/[eventId]/vendors/[vendorId]` shows `[Cancel booking]` CTA when `event_vendors.status='contracted'` AND no `service_order_payments` row exists with `confirmed_at IS NOT NULL` for this vendor's bookings on this event. Click → confirmation modal → hard-delete `event_vendors` row + notification to vendor chat thread per [0019](0019_communications/0019_communications.md) + email per [0028](0028_email_notifications/0028_email_notifications.md) template `host_cancelled_booking` + date frees on vendor's calendar via `vendor_calendar_blocks` cleanup. Reversible (host can re-add via marketplace). Cancel CTA **HIDDEN** when `status='deposit_paid'` or later · replaced with `[Request refund/dispute]` CTA opening existing [0023 § 3.6 Disputes](0023_admin_console/0023_admin_console.md) flow. **Rule 2 · Vendor-side release pre-downpayment.** Vendor's `/vendor-dashboard/clients/[event_id]` page shows `[Release this booking]` CTA when no confirmed downpayment exists. Click → confirmation modal explaining host will be notified → `event_vendors` row hard-deletes + audit row inserts into NEW `vendor_release_history` table (release_id PK · event_vendor_id FK preserve-on-delete via separate column snapshot · vendor_profile_id · vendor_user_id · host_user_id · event_id snapshot · release_reason TEXT · vendor_notes TEXT NULL · released_at TIMESTAMPTZ) + chat thread notification + email per 0028 template `vendor_released_booking` to host + host's planning surface auto-refreshes with polite "{Vendor} couldn't take your booking after all — here are 3 similar vendors" suggestion strip pulling from existing 5-tier ranking ladder per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-24 seventh row. Vendor CANNOT release confirmed (downpaid) booking unilaterally · same as host side · dispute path only. Per owner-picked answer Q4: **free release, audit-logged only · no strike system · no release fee** · matches PH market reality where vendors politely back out routinely · `vendor_release_history` accumulates trend data for V1.x admin pattern analysis (10+ releases per vendor per month flags admin review for ghosting pattern). **Rule 3 · Pre-downpayment overlap default — vendor-configurable hold limit per date.** Per owner-picked answer Q2 ("Vendor sets a hold limit · e.g., max 3 per date"): new column `vendor_profiles.max_soft_holds_per_date INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 3 CHECK (max_soft_holds_per_date BETWEEN 1 AND 20)`. When host clicks Lock on a vendor via `finalizeVendor` server action, action checks count of existing `event_vendors` rows with same `vendor_profile_id` (joined via marketplace_vendor_id) + same event date (joined via events.wedding_date) + status='contracted' + archived_at IS NULL. If count >= `max_soft_holds_per_date`, action returns new status `'soft_hold_limit_reached'` with vendor's current limit + suggestion strip of 3 similar vendors. Vendor's `/vendor-dashboard/settings/availability` surface lets vendor adjust limit per-account-wide. Future V1.x: per-date override toggle on vendor's calendar (block this specific date from new inquiries · or raise/lower limit for this date only). Vendor sees badge `N soft holds` per date on `/vendor-dashboard/calendar` + expandable list of host names + event dates + "considering since" timestamps. **Rule 4 · Downpayment confirmation auto-releases other soft holds.** Per owner-picked answer Q3 ("Auto-release all others on downpayment"): when admin reconciles a downpayment via existing 0034 § 3.3 admin payment-confirm flow AND the downpayment links to an `event_vendor.event_vendor_id` (the existing payment-line-item → event-vendor mapping), system queries `event_vendors` for OTHER rows where same `vendor_profile_id` (joined via marketplace_vendor_id) + same event date (via events.wedding_date join) + status='contracted' + archived_at IS NULL + vendor_id != the confirming row's vendor_id. For each found row: hard-delete `event_vendors` + insert `vendor_release_history` audit row with release_reason='auto_released_on_downpayment' + send notification per 0028 template `auto_released_due_to_other_booking` to affected host + host's planning surface auto-refreshes with similar-vendors suggestion strip. Vendor gets summary notification: "Couple A's downpayment confirmed for {date} · released N other soft holds automatically · review vendor_release_history if needed." No fallback option (owner chose auto-release over manual decide-per-row · simpler UX · removes vendor's safety-net workflow but eliminates ghost holds completely · aligns with platform-discipline arc from CLAUDE.md 2026-05-22 row 11 vendor reputation guardrails). **Rule 5 · Schedule-block primitive auto-created on hard lock.** Already speced per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20 row "Layout: Event-home planning cards" lock for `vendor_calendar_blocks` (30-min granularity per existing iteration 0022 spec). Once admin reconciles downpayment + Rule 4 fires, system also auto-creates a calendar block on vendor's `/vendor-dashboard/calendar` for the wedding window (start = wedding_date + venue_setup_hour · end = wedding_date + venue_teardown_hour · block_label = "Confirmed: {Couple Names}" · block_source='setnayan_booking' · is_private=FALSE so vendor's team can see it). Block links back to the `event_vendors` row · click → opens vendor's per-event workspace. **(3) Schema additions** (queued for migration · push BEFORE merge per [[feedback_setnayan_push_migrations_myself]]): `ALTER TABLE vendor_profiles ADD COLUMN max_soft_holds_per_date INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 3 CHECK (max_soft_holds_per_date BETWEEN 1 AND 20)` · `CREATE TABLE vendor_release_history` (10 columns per Rule 2 above · index on `(vendor_profile_id, released_at DESC)` for V1.x admin pattern queries · RLS: vendor reads their own rows · admin reads all rows · host reads their own event's rows for audit transparency). **(4) finalizeVendor server action extensions:** new return status `'soft_hold_limit_reached'` (per Rule 3) · existing 'hard_single_conflict' + 'already_locked' + 'not_found' + 'error' all preserved · UI handling in `plan-card-compare.tsx` performLock + `vendor-pick-grid-card.tsx` + `vendor-pick-card.tsx` for the new status (modal: "This vendor already has {N} confirmed soft holds for {date} · {Vendor} only takes {limit} simultaneous holds · here are 3 similar vendors who can take this date" + suggestion strip). **New server actions:** `cancelBookingAsHost(event_id, vendor_id)` (Rule 1 path · idempotent · returns 'already_deleted' if row missing OR 'downpaid_use_dispute_flow' if past soft-hold gate) · `releaseBookingAsVendor(event_id, vendor_id, reason, notes)` (Rule 2 path · vendor-authorized via existing vendor_team_members RLS · idempotent same shape). **Auto-trigger on payment confirmation:** new database trigger OR server-side cron-free sweep on `service_order_payments.confirmed_at` insert/update · checks for `event_vendor_id` linkage · fires Rule 4 cleanup if conditions met · idempotent on re-confirmation. **(5) UI surfaces:** Host side — `/dashboard/[eventId]/vendors/[vendorId]` gains conditional `[Cancel booking]` CTA per Rule 1 (status check + payment check). Locked Booster catalog from owner screenshot: **4 Bidding Tokens** → Radius boost (Free vendor expands radius from 10km to next tier's 20km · OR Verified vendor expands to 50km · for 7 days) · **10 Bidding Tokens** → Packages boost (Phase L1 spec ambiguity: unlock additional package slots beyond tier default OR feature a specific package at top of search · owner to clarify · most likely "featured package" pin) · **25 Bidding Tokens** → Chat boost (Phase L1 ambiguity: priority response queue OR premium chat appearance OR pinned-vendor-in-couple's-inbox · owner to clarify) · **50 Bidding Tokens** → Video Call boost (Free/Verified vendor unlocks PeerJS video call ability for 7 days OR per-call · Phase L1 picks the unit) · **100 Bidding Tokens** → Scheduling boost (Free vendor upgrades from Manual to Hybrid Scheduling for 7 days). All boosters consume tokens from vendor's existing `vendor_wallets` (purchased + 45-day-expiring earned vouchers · baseline ₱250/token per V2 blueprint · free vendors can buy token packs at 4/10/25/50/100 denominations). Boosters are STACK-AWARE: a Free vendor with active Radius Booster + active Video Call Booster runs effectively at Verified-radius + Pro-video for the booster window. The 17% discount anchor matches typical SaaS annual-vs-monthly conventions (Notion 16% · Linear 20% · Webflow 20% · Stripe Atlas 20% · Shopify 25%) · sits mid-range · doesn't anchor cheap (>20%) doesn't anchor stingy (<10%). The ₱19,999 + ₱54,999 charm-priced endings match the locked Pricing.md § 1 charm convention from CLAUDE.md 2026-05-12 row (-1 endings on round prices). **(8) Verification-fee retirement rationale.** Per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-16 row 8 the verification fees were modeled as ongoing-cost defense (admin labor + KYC API + sanctions screening = ~₱535/vendor + ~₱200/yr recurring per Persona/Veriff/Onfido renewal). v2.1's one-time lifetime badge reframes verification as a CAC investment (Setnayan absorbs the ~₱535 once · earns it back via Pro/Enterprise subscription LTV · no recurring vendor fee needed). Demotion-recovery fee retirement reflects that disputes already route through 0023 § 6 with admin moderation · adding a re-verification fee is redundant friction on already-disciplined vendors (the demotion itself is the consequence · no need to double-tax with a fee). Net financial impact: Setnayan forgoes ₱1,499/yr × verified vendor count (e.g., 1,000 verified vendors = ₱1.5M/yr foregone) BUT gains LTV via Pro/Enterprise subscription stickiness from the annual discount mechanic · trade is roughly margin-neutral at scale + simplifies the vendor onboarding pitch (one fee, one badge, forever). **(9) Affected files** (spec corpus this row · engineering deferred to Phase L8). | 2026-05-28 | **Twelfth 2026-05-28 row · perf optimization shipped via PR [#567](https://github.com/iscasasola/setnayan-platform/pull/567) · event-home `/dashboard/[eventId]` 4 sequential round trips → 2 · ~150-600ms TTFB win on every render.** Owner asked why auto-login to dashboard loads materially slower than Facebook home page. Diagnosed against the 1976-line event-home server component as 4 sequential Supabase round trips before first paint: Round 1 (top Promise.all · 18 queries · parallel) → Round 2 (`compatibilityFetches` · 4 queries · parallel) → Round 3 (SERIAL `vendor_services` cross-category fetch) → Round 6 (SERIAL `[fetchEventActivity, fetchAttributedActivity]` Promise.all) → Round 7 (SERIAL `fetchUpcomingItems`). **Fix:** lifted the three serial awaits into the existing parallel rounds — `fetchEventActivity` + `fetchAttributedActivity` into round 1 (only need `eventId` + `user.id` available at start) · cross-category `vendor_services` fetch into round 2 (depends only on `marketplaceIds` from round 1, ready BEFORE compat lookups) · `fetchUpcomingItems` into round 2 (depends only on `event.event_date` + `event.ceremony_type` from round 1's `eventRes`). Net: 4 sequential rounds → 2. At Supabase Singapore RTT ~50-200ms from PH, saves ~150-600ms on every event-home render. **Safety:** same `.catch()` / IIFE try/catch with `logQueryError` + safe-default shapes as the existing fetchers (6th hotfix pass · Path B 2026-05-23) · a throw in any single fetcher degrades just that lane to empty data (same as today) · same admin-client gating for cross-category services + attributed activity (the parent `event_vendors` / `event_action_log` queries already enforce the host's RLS · admin reads are safe). **No schema change** · no new dependencies · no UX change · `+142/-91` net diff on `apps/web/app/dashboard/[eventId]/page.tsx` · `pnpm typecheck` + `pnpm lint` clean. **Comparison framing for the owner question:** Facebook home loads faster because of global CDN + warm edge servers + decade of streaming-hydration tuning — Setnayan can't match that, but the 3 of 4 round trips that were stacked sequentially for no architectural reason within Setnayan's own stack are now collapsed.
